36	| 2026-06-23 | **SD write buffers must be cache-line aligned (`__ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE)`, 32 B) or writes drop to ~10x-slow single-sector transfers.** First `sd bench` on hardware: read 5.7 MB/s but write **0.4 MB/s** (verify ok). Root cause is in the generated FatFs diskio (`system/fs/fat_fs/hardware_access/diskio.c`): for a buffer not aligned to `CACHE_LINE_SIZE`, `disk_write` bounces through a `SYS_FS_FAT_ALIGNED_BUFFER_LEN`-sized (512 B = **one sector**) buffer in a loop → single-sector writes; `disk_read` for the same unaligned buffer still does a single multi-block transfer (reads sector 0 via the bounce buffer, the rest directly into the app buffer) → stays fast. Built `u-boot.bin` from `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig` (macOS: `gmake`, OpenSSL via the **environment** so dtc's bundled-libfdt include isn't clobbered). **Validated on hardware: marvin boots standalone from NAND** (RomBOOT → at91bootstrap copies `0x100000` from `0x40000` → marvin runs, HDMI captured). | Closes the 2026-06-09 "macOS-native NAND is Phase-2 R&D" item. OpenOCD's `at91sam9` NAND driver can't do PMECC, so it can't write a bootable boot region; u-boot's driver uses the same PMECC IP and its DT (hw ECC, **8-bit/512, eccOffset 152** = `oobsize − 8·13`) matches both the chip's ONFI (`nand info`: 4096/256/8/512) and the at91bootstrap header generator — so `nand write` is RomBOOT-correct. **Two non-obvious gotchas, both bench-found:** (1) The SAM9X7 ROM reads page 0 *without ECC* expecting a NAND header — 52 copies of a 32-bit word, code at offset `0xD0` (DS60001813D p.159/162). SAM-BA's `writeboot` synthesizes this; a plain `nand write` does not, so headerless writes give RomBOOT-only (no boot). Fix: prepend the header with `binaries/make-pmecchead.sh` (wraps at91bootstrap `addpmecchead.py`) using the **real** chip params → word `0xc2605007`; *not* that script's SAM9X7 defaults (2048/64/4), which don't match this board. ```text
#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata

The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:

- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.

**Storage split (decided).** The line is drawn by *what the data is coupled to*, not by convenience:

- **Compile-time, in flash:** recognizer templates/signatures (centroids, menu baselines, song bitmap templates, thresholds) **and** the menu graph. These are *algorithm-coupled* — a template is only valid paired with the exact grid geometry, sampling, and normalization compiled into the C recognizer, and is re-learned in lockstep when the algorithm changes. They are generated from the host corpus by `tools/gameplay/gameplay/export_c.py` into `gameplay_metadata.h` and consumed through pointers by `gameplay_classify.c` / `gameplay_select.c`. **Recognition never reads the SD card** — so a missing or stale card can never cause a silent misclassification.
- **On the SD card (`/marvin/games/<game>/songs.json`):** the song catalog *labels* — the human-meaningful, user-editable metadata that changes independently of the firmware. Keyed by the stable `(setlist, index)` identifier the recognizer already emits (`gp_song_t`):

```json
{
  "game": "gh3-wii",
  "metadata_version": "<stamp matching the firmware build>",
  "songs": [
    { "setlist": "main", "index": 4, "title": "...", "artist": "...", "bpm": 120, "length_s": 210 }
  ]
}
```

The catalog is *labels only* — recognition does not depend on it; a missing/stale catalog degrades to "Unknown song", never a functional break. `export_c.py` also emits a `metadata_version` `#define` into `gameplay_metadata.h`; the same value goes in `songs.json` so the UI can warn if the catalog predates a template-set regeneration. Because the catalog is keyed by `(setlist, index)`, a mismatch degrades gracefully rather than misclassifying.

Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.

31	static void iso8601_utc(char *buf, size_t n)
32	{
33	    struct tm t;
34	    memset(&t, 0, sizeof(t));
35	    RTC_TimeGet(&t);
36	    (void)snprintf(buf, n, "%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d:%02dZ",
37	                   t.tm_year + 1900, t.tm_mon + 1, t.tm_mday,
38	                   t.tm_hour, t.tm_min, t.tm_sec);
39	}
40	
41	/* Write s into out as a quoted CSV field ("..."), doubling any embedded quote.
42	 * Always quoted, so embedded commas are safe. Truncates to fit. */
43	static void csv_quote(const char *s, char *out, size_t n)
44	{
45	    size_t j = 0;
46	    if (n == 0) { return; }
47	    if (s == NULL) { s = ""; }
48	
49	    if (j < n - 1) { out[j++] = '"'; }
50	    for (size_t i = 0; s[i] != '\0' && j < n - 2; i++)
51	    {
52	        if (s[i] == '"' && j < n - 3) { out[j++] = '"'; }   /* escape by doubling */
53	        out[j++] = s[i];
54	    }
55	    if (j < n - 1) { out[j++] = '"'; }
56	    out[j] = '\0';
57	}
58	
59	/* Split a CSV line in place into fields[], honoring double-quoted fields
60	 * (commas inside quotes, "" -> "). Returns the field count. */
61	static int csv_split(char *line, char *fields[], int maxf)
62	{
63	    int nf = 0;
64	    char *p = line;
65	
66	    while (nf < maxf)
67	    {
68	        if (*p == '"')
69	        {
70	            p++;
71	            char *w = p;            /* unescape in place */
72	            fields[nf++] = w;
73	            while (*p != '\0')
74	            {
75	                if (*p == '"')
76	                {
77	                    if (p[1] == '"') { *w++ = '"'; p += 2; }
78	                    else { p++; break; }   /* closing quote */
79	                }
80	                else { *w++ = *p++; }
81	            }
82	            *w = '\0';
83	            while (*p != '\0' && *p != ',' && *p != '\n' && *p != '\r') { p++; }
84	        }
85	        else
86	        {
87	            fields[nf++] = p;
88	            while (*p != '\0' && *p != ',' && *p != '\n' && *p != '\r') { p++; }
89	        }
90	
91	        if (*p == ',') { *p = '\0'; p++; }
92	        else { *p = '\0'; break; }
93	    }
94	    return nf;
95	}
96	
97	/* ---- player ------------------------------------------------------------- */
98	
99	void Results_Initialize(void)
100	{
101	    /* Default player is the static initializer; nothing else to set up. */
102	}
103	
104	void Results_SetPlayer(const char *name)
105	{
106	    if (name == NULL || name[0] == '\0') { return; }
107	
108	    size_t j = 0;
109	    for (size_t i = 0; name[i] != '\0' && j < sizeof(s_player) - 1; i++)
110	    {
111	        char c = name[i];
112	        if (c == ',' || c == '"' || c == '\n' || c == '\r') { continue; }
113	        s_player[j++] = c;
114	    }
115	    s_player[j] = '\0';
116	}
117	
118	const char *Results_GetPlayer(void) { return s_player; }
119	
120	/* ---- append ------------------------------------------------------------- */
121	
122	bool Results_Append(const results_record_t *rec)
123	{
124	    if (rec == NULL) { return false; }
125	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return false; }
126	
127	    char dir[64];
128	    build_path(dir, sizeof(dir), RES_REL_DIR);
129	    (void)SYS_FS_DirectoryMake(dir);   /* harmless if it already exists */
130	
131	    char path[80];
132	    build_path(path, sizeof(path), RES_REL_FILE);
133	
134	    bool need_header = true;
135	    SYS_FS_FSTAT st;
136	    if (SYS_FS_FileStat(path, &st) == SYS_FS_RES_SUCCESS && st.fsize > 0u)
137	    {
138	        need_header = false;
139	    }
140	
141	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_APPEND);
142	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
143	    {
144	        LOG_WARN("RES: open append failed (fs err %d)\r\n", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
145	        return false;
146	    }
147	
148	    char line[RES_LINE_MAX];
149	    int len;
150	
151	    if (need_header)
152	    {
153	        len = snprintf(line, sizeof(line), "%s\n", RES_HEADER);
154	        if (len > 0 && (size_t)len < sizeof(line))
155	        {
156	            (void)SYS_FS_FileWrite(h, line, (size_t)len);
157	        }
158	    }
159	
160	    char ts[24];
161	    iso8601_utc(ts, sizeof(ts));
162	
163	    char song_q[96];
164	    csv_quote(rec->song, song_q, sizeof(song_q));
165	
166	    len = snprintf(line, sizeof(line),
167	                   "%s,%s,%s,%u,%s,%s,%s,%lu,%u.%u,%u,%u,%s\n",
168	                   s_player,
169	                   (rec->game != NULL) ? rec->game : "",
170	                   (rec->setlist != NULL) ? rec->setlist : "",
171	                   (unsigned)rec->index,
172	                   song_q,
173	                   (rec->difficulty != NULL) ? rec->difficulty : "",
174	                   (rec->part != NULL) ? rec->part : "",
175	                   (unsigned long)rec->score,
176	                   (unsigned)(rec->accuracy_x10 / 10u), (unsigned)(rec->accuracy_x10 % 10u),
177	                   (unsigned)rec->notes_hit,
178	                   (unsigned)rec->notes_total,
179	                   ts);
180	
181	    bool ok = false;
182	    if (len > 0 && (size_t)len < sizeof(line))
183	    {
184	        ok = (SYS_FS_FileWrite(h, line, (size_t)len) == (size_t)len);
185	    }
186	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
187	    return ok;
188	}
189	
190	/* ---- top-N read --------------------------------------------------------- */
191	
192	int Results_TopN(const char *setlist, uint8_t index, const char *difficulty,
193	                 results_score_t *out, int max)
194	{
195	    if (out == NULL || max <= 0 || setlist == NULL) { return 0; }
196	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0; }
197	
198	    char path[80];
199	    build_path(path, sizeof(path), RES_REL_FILE);
200	
201	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
202	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID) { return 0; }
203	
204	    int  count = 0;
205	    bool first = true;
206	    char line[RES_LINE_MAX];
207	
208	    while (!SYS_FS_FileEOF(h))
209	    {
210	        if (SYS_FS_FileStringGet(h, line, sizeof(line)) != SYS_FS_RES_SUCCESS) { break; }
211	        if (first) { first = false; continue; }     /* header row */
212	        if (line[0] == '\0' || line[0] == '\n' || line[0] == '\r') { continue; }
213	
214	        char *f[RES_FIELDS];
215	        if (csv_split(line, f, RES_FIELDS) < RES_FIELDS) { continue; }
216	
217	        if (strcmp(f[2], setlist) != 0) { continue; }
218	        if ((unsigned)atoi(f[3]) != (unsigned)index) { continue; }
219	        if (difficulty != NULL && difficulty[0] != '\0' &&
220	            strcmp(f[5], difficulty) != 0) { continue; }
221	
222	        uint32_t score = (uint32_t)strtoul(f[7], NULL, 10);
223	
224	        /* Insert into the bounded, score-descending top list. */
225	        int pos = count;
226	        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++)
227	        {
228	            if (score > out[i].score) { pos = i; break; }
229	        }
230	        if (pos >= max) { continue; }
231	
232	        int last = (count < max) ? count : (max - 1);
233	        for (int i = last; i > pos; i--) { out[i] = out[i - 1]; }
234	
235	        strncpy(out[pos].player, f[0], sizeof(out[pos].player) - 1);
236	        out[pos].player[sizeof(out[pos].player) - 1] = '\0';
237	        strncpy(out[pos].timestamp, f[11], sizeof(out[pos].timestamp) - 1);
238	        out[pos].timestamp[sizeof(out[pos].timestamp) - 1] = '\0';
239	        out[pos].score = score;
240	
241	        if (count < max) { count++; }
242	    }
243	
244	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
245	    return count;
246	}
247
```

7	/* Per-player gameplay results -> <card>/players/results.csv (spec §4.8.6).
8	 *
9	 * Flat, append-only CSV: one row per completed run, header row on first write.
10	 * Marvin reads it back on-device for high scores; the card is also taken to a
11	 * PC for analysis (pandas/Excel). CSV is the format that serves both — on-device
12	 * it parses with comma-splitting + atol into static buffers (no malloc, no JSON
13	 * tokenizer), which fits FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1 and the static-allocation rule.
14	 *
15	 * Builds entirely on the SD/FatFs/RTC layer (storage.c); no gameplay dependency,
16	 * so the write + read + display path is testable now with synthetic rows. The
17	 * gameplay engine wires in later by filling a record and calling Results_Append
18	 * once the M9 Phase 3 score readers exist. */
19

7	/* SD-card storage: owns the FAT mount lifecycle and the bring-up diagnostics.
8	 *
9	 * Mounting is manual for now — DRV_SDMMC uses polled card detection and SYS_FS
10	 * automount is disabled, so the app issues SYS_FS_Mount itself. The mount
11	 * trigger is isolated in Storage_Mount()/Storage_Unmount() so it can later be
12	 * replaced by a SYS_FS mount/unmount event handler (for hotplug) without
13	 * touching the diagnostics, which depend only on Storage_IsMounted() and the
14	 * mount-point string.
15	 *
16	 * The mount path uses SYS_FS calls that block on SD I/O, so Storage_Mount and
17	 * every Storage_Diag* must be called from a task (after the scheduler is up),
18	 * not from APP_Initialize. */
19	
20	void Storage_Initialize(void);

22	/* Mount the SD volume. Bounded internal retry — after insertion the polling
23	 * driver needs a moment before SYS_FS reports the media ready. Idempotent:

34	/* Bring-up diagnostics (driven by the `sd` console command). Each mounts on

#ifndef GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H
#define GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "queue.h"

/* Game-state observer — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.8 (M9).
 *
 * A video-frame consumer (not a detector): it classifies which GH3 screen the
 * captured frame shows and publishes typed game_state_t events on its own bus
 * (xGameStateQueue), kept separate from the detector-state bus per the §4.2
 * multi-detector decision. The recognizer data (region grid, per-class
 * centroids, thresholds) is the host-proven metadata frozen into
 * game/gameplay_metadata.h by `gameplay export-c`.
 *
 * Phase 1 (this module): screen classification only. Selection/song readers
 * (Phase 2) and the navigator/controller (Phase 3, M10) build on this. */

typedef struct
{
    uint32_t frame_epoch;   /* master sync token, = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count */
    uint64_t timestamp_us;  /* monotonic, marvin-local */
    uint8_t  screen;        /* GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN */
    uint8_t  reserved[3];
    int32_t  best_dist;     /* L1 to the nearest centroid */
    int32_t  margin;        /* second-best − best (confidence) */
    int16_t  selection;     /* static-list cell, song-template index, or -1 (none) */
} game_state_t;

/* Brings up the game-state bus queue and the observer task. The observer
 * subscribes to the video frame queue from inside its task, so call this after
 * Video_Initialize. Observation starts disabled; call SetObserveEnabled(true)
 * to begin publishing (spec §6 game_observe_enable). */
void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void);

/* Game-state event bus. Consumers (operator UI, the controller at M10) read
 * here. Returns NULL until GameplayEngine_Initialize has run. */
QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void);

/* Observation toggle. When off the task still drains frames (so the video
 * queue doesn't back up) but classifies nothing and emits no events. */
void GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(bool on);
bool GameplayEngine_ObserveEnabled(void);

/* Force the observer to run on the next captured frame, bypassing the ~5 Hz
 * background rate limit. Intended for closed-loop control (M10): read the result
 * of an actuator command promptly instead of waiting for the next background
 * tick. One-shot (cleared once consumed); thread-safe (single volatile flag).
 *
 * NOTE: don't trigger this the instant after sending the command — GH3 menus
 * take several frames to transition (cursor animation, screen fades, a `loading`
 * screen). The caller should let the screen settle first (a delay, and/or poll
 * until the expected screen appears with a timeout) rather than trust a single
 * immediate read. That settle policy lives in the controller (M10). */
void GameplayEngine_RequestObservation(void);

/* Most recently classified screen (GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN);
 * GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN before the first classified frame. */
uint8_t GameplayEngine_CurrentScreen(void);

#endif

```text
=== spec 4.8.6/4.8.7 ===
#### 4.8.6 Performance results & player profiles 🚧

Per-player gameplay results, stored on the SD card as `/marvin/players/results.csv` — a flat,
append-only CSV (one row per completed run, with a header row). Keyed to a song by the same
`(setlist, index)` the recognizer emits:

```
player,game,setlist,index,song,difficulty,part,score,accuracy_pct,notes_hit,notes_total,timestamp
greg,gh3-wii,main,4,"Slow Ride",hard,lead,123456,92.4,480,520,2026-06-23T23:14:00Z
```

**Why CSV (not JSON/YAML or a DB).** Results have two consumers — Marvin reads `results.csv` to show
high scores on-device, and the card is taken to a PC for deeper analysis. CSV is the only format that
serves both well: on-device it parses with comma-splitting + `atol` into static buffers (no malloc,
no JSON tokenizer, stream one line at a time — fits `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1` and the static-allocation
rule); on a PC it's a one-liner in pandas/Excel/awk. JSONL is nicer for nested/evolving schemas but
costs an on-device tokenizer for no benefit here (results are flat and tabular); YAML has no good
zero-alloc embedded parser; a DB (SQLite) needs malloc + a FatFs VFS shim — overkill for an
append-only log. Schema evolution: append columns at the end (the on-device reader touches only the
columns it needs; pandas keys by header). The `song` title is duplicated alongside `(setlist,index)`
so the CSV is self-contained for analysis without joining the catalog.

Scope boundary: `results.csv` is the **flat per-run summary** only. Deep per-note / per-section
telemetry belongs in the recording subsystem (§4.6 `state.bin`), keeping this file trivially
parseable on-device.

On-device high scores: scan the file, filter by `(setlist, index[, difficulty])`, keep a fixed
top-N array in static memory. A full scan per display is fine at expected scale (hundreds–thousands
of rows ≈ tens–hundreds of KB); if it ever grows large, cap the log or maintain a small separate
high-score cache.

Dependencies and open points:

- **Score/accuracy capture depends on the number/score readers — M9 Phase 3**, not yet started. Until
  those land, only the song identity + difficulty/part are recordable. The CSV writer + on-device
  top-N reader + a `scores` console command can be built and validated now against synthetic rows,
  since they sit entirely on the proven SD/FatFs/RTC layer (§4.6.2, §4.8.7-adjacent).
- **`timestamp` is UTC from the RTC** (§4.7), confirmed persistent across power cycles. FAT has no
  timezone field, so file mtimes are also written in UTC by convention.
- **Player identity** is a simple operator-entered string for now (e.g. a `player` console command
  setting the current name); richer profiles are out of scope. Tracked as Q12.

#### 4.8.7 Album artwork 🚧

Per-song cover art for the operator UI, stored on the SD card as standard **JPEG or PNG** (so the files are viewable on any workstation) under `/marvin/games/<game>/art/`. Named by the same stable recognizer key as the catalog, so firmware derives the path directly — no `songs.json` lookup, no dependency on the catalog being present:

```
art/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     // e.g. art/main-04.jpg, art/bonus-12.png  (NN = zero-padded index)
```

**Pre-cache at startup, not per-use.** After the FAT mount (M4), the firmware walks `art/` and decodes every image **once** into a static, pre-allocated cache of fixed-size slots in DDR; runtime artwork access is then an O(1) pointer into RAM — no card I/O, no decode, and no allocation at use time (consistent with the static-allocation rule). A missing/oversized/corrupt file leaves its slot empty → UI placeholder.

- **Decoder — Legato's own runtime decoders; no new library.** JPEG (built-in) and PNG (lodepng) are already enabled in this project (`legato_config.h`: `LE_ENABLE_JPEG_DECODER=1`, `LE_ENABLE_PNG_DECODER=1`). Because `LE_STREAMING_ENABLED=0`, the flow is: read the whole compressed file into a RAM buffer → point a `leImage` (`LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG` / `_PNG`) at it → decode into the cache slot via the Legato image API. Source images authored at the target WxH decode 1:1 (no scaling).
- **Cache pixel format & size.** A decoded Legato raster; **RGBA8888** is the natural full-color choice, **RGB_565** (already used by the project's other assets) halves the RAM cost if alpha isn't needed. Cache = `N_songs × W × H × bytes/px`; for ~70 songs at RGBA8888 that's ≈ 4.5 MB (128×128) / 11 MB (200×200) / 18 MB (256×256), all comfortable in the SAM9X75D2G's DDR (framebuffers use only a few MB). On-card JPEGs total ≈ 1.5–3 MB.
- **Exact target dimensions + cache pixel format** are settled when the Legato artwork UI slot is designed. Tracked as Q13.

### 4.9 Operator command console ✅

```md
# Song catalog loader (marvin, spec §4.8.3)

## Context

The marvin recognizer identifies a selected GH3 song as a `gp_song_t {setlist, index, tmpl}`
(`game/gameplay_select.h`). The compile-time templates in `game/gameplay_metadata.h` carry only a
machine slug (`song_id`, e.g. `"slow_ride"`) — no human title, artist, BPM, or length. So the UI and
the high-score display can only show `main #4`, not "Slow Ride".

The catalog loader closes that gap: it maps the recognizer's stable `(setlist, index)` key →
human-meaningful labels read from the SD card, so a missing/stale catalog degrades to "Unknown song"
but **never** affects recognition (recognition stays compile-time in flash). It is the next SD
consumer after `storage`/`time`/`results`, and is buildable now — it keys off data that already
exists, with no dependency on the rest of the gameplay engine being resolved.

**Decisions settled with Greg this session:**
- **Format = flat CSV** (`songs.csv`), not the JSON the spec currently names — same rationale that
  moved `results` to CSV (no on-device JSON tokenizer, `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, static buffers; opens in
  pandas/Excel). Spec §4.8.3 gets reconciled to CSV.
- **Stale-version check deferred.** `gameplay_metadata.h` does not emit a `GP_METADATA_VERSION`
  define yet (the generated header would need `export_c.py` to add it). Build the core lookup now;
  the loader degrades to "Unknown song" on any miss regardless. The stale-warning lands later once
  `export_c.py` stamps the version. Tracked as an open item.

## CSV format — `<card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`

\```
setlist,index,title,artist,bpm,length_s
main,0,"Slow Ride","Foghat",0,0
main,4,"Rock and Roll All Nite","Kiss",0,0
bonus,24,"Through the Fire and Flames","DragonForce",0,0
\```

- `setlist` is the string `main`/`bonus` (human-editable, matches `results.csv`); mapped to the
  numeric `GP_SETLIST_MAIN`/`GP_SETLIST_BONUS` on load.
- `title`/`artist` are CSV-quoted (may contain commas); parsed with the shared quote-aware splitter.
- `bpm`/`length_s` are optional integers (0 = unknown). Rows may be sparse / out of order; only
  `(setlist, index)` need be unique.
- Header row required; the loader skips it. Path is `Storage_MountPoint()`-relative, exactly like
  `results` (`players/results.csv`), so it lands under `games/gh3-wii/` at the card root.

## Approach

**Lazy-loaded static cache** (deviates from `results`' per-call streaming, justified): catalog lookups
during menu navigation / high-score display are frequent and read-mostly, and `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`
means we should not hold the catalog file open while `results.csv` is open. Load the whole catalog
once into a static array (bounded by `GP_N_SONGS = 64`) on first use; lookups are then O(n) in RAM
with the file closed. Footprint ≈ 64 × ~120 B ≈ 8 KB BSS — fine under the static-allocation rule.

### Files

1. **`default/src/util/csv.{h,c}` (new)** — extract `csv_split` (quote-aware, in-place) and
   `csv_quote` verbatim from `results/results.c` into a shared util, so the catalog reader reuses the
   proven splitter instead of duplicating it. `results.c` then includes `util/csv.h` and drops its
   two static copies (only non-behavioral change to a just-shipped file).

2. **`default/src/game/catalog.{h,c}` (new)** — the loader. Lives in `game/` next to
   `gameplay_select.h`/`gameplay_metadata.h` since it is keyed by `GP_SETLIST_*` / `gp_song_t`.

   \```c
   typedef struct {
       uint8_t  setlist;        /* GP_SETLIST_* */
       uint8_t  index;
       char     title[64];
       char     artist[48];
       uint16_t bpm;            /* 0 = unknown */
       uint16_t length_s;       /* 0 = unknown */
   } catalog_entry_t;

   void Catalog_Initialize(void);                                   /* state only, no I/O */
   bool Catalog_Lookup(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index,
                       catalog_entry_t *out);                       /* lazy-loads on first call */
   bool Catalog_LookupSong(const gp_song_t *song, catalog_entry_t *out); /* convenience wrapper */
   bool Catalog_Reload(void);                                       /* force reload after card swap */
   int  Catalog_Count(void);                                        /* entries currently cached */
   bool Catalog_IsLoaded(void);
   \```

   - Internals mirror `results.c`: `build_path()` off `Storage_MountPoint()`, `Storage_Mount()` on
     demand, `SYS_FS_FileOpen(READ)`, `SYS_FS_FileStringGet` line loop, `csv_split` into fields,
     `atoi`/`strtoul` for numerics, all into a file-scope `static catalog_entry_t s_entries[GP_N_SONGS]`.
   - Local `setlist_id(const char*)` maps `"main"`/`"bonus"` → numeric (unknown row → skipped).
   - Load failure (no card / no file) leaves the cache empty and `Catalog_Lookup` returns false →
     caller shows "Unknown song". Never fatal.

3. **`default/src/console/console.c`** — add a `catalog` command mirroring `cmd_scores`/`cmd_sd`:
   - `catalog reload` → `Catalog_Reload()`, print count.
   - `catalog ls` → list cached `(setlist index — title / artist)`.
   - `catalog <main|bonus> <index>` → lookup + print one entry (or "Unknown song").
   Add one row to the `bindings[]` table (line ~485, next to `scores`/`results`).

4. **`default/src/app.c`** — call `Catalog_Initialize()` alongside `Results_Initialize()` (~line 174).

5. **`cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`** — add `game/catalog.c` and `util/csv.c` to the source list
   (next to `results/results.c`, line ~20).

6. **`firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv` (new, seed)** — a starter catalog generated from
   the 64 `song_id` slugs in `gameplay_metadata.h` (slug → humanized title), `artist`/`bpm`/`length_s`
   left blank/0 as clearly-placeholder fields for Greg to fill and copy onto the card. Marked as a

7. **`docs/spec.md` §4.8.3** — reconcile JSON → CSV: replace the `songs.json` block with the

   framing, and note the `metadata_version` stamp as deferred-until-`export_c.py`-emits-it.

8. **`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`** — decision-log entry (CSV catalog, lazy static cache, shared
   `csv` util, deferred version check) + update the "Next up: song catalog" focus note to reflect it
   landed. Add the deferred `GP_METADATA_VERSION` / stale-warning as an open item.

## Out of scope / deferred
- `GP_METADATA_VERSION` emission in `export_c.py` and the stale-catalog UI warning (deferred above).
- Album artwork pre-cache (spec §4.8.7, separate workstream; the art path is derived directly from

  3. `catalog ls` → rows print with titles/artists.
  4. `catalog main 4` → prints the matching title (or "Unknown song" if absent).
  5. `catalog main 99` → "Unknown song" (graceful miss).
  6. Remove the file / unmount → `catalog reload` → count 0, lookups return "Unknown song" (never
     hangs or faults).
- **Degradation invariant:** with no card or no `songs.csv`, the firmware still boots and every other
  subsystem is unaffected (catalog is labels-only).

## We do have a plan — spec §4.8.7

Album art is already specced, and crucially it's **decoupled from the catalog by design**:

```
<card>/games/gh3-wii/art/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}    e.g. art/main-04.jpg, art/bonus-12.png
```

- Named by the **same `(setlist, index)` key** the recognizer emits → firmware derives the path directly. **No catalog lookup, no dependency on `songs.csv` being present.**
- Pre-cached once at startup into fixed-size DDR slots (Legato's built-in JPEG/PNG decoders, no new lib). Missing/corrupt file → empty slot → UI placeholder.

So the two live as siblings under `games/<game>/`, which my catalog plan already creates:

```
games/gh3-wii/
  songs.csv          ← catalog (labels: title/artist/bpm/length)
  art/               ← artwork (keyed by setlist-NN)
```

## On your two points

**"Will metadata support it?"** — It doesn't need to, and deliberately shouldn't. Both the catalog row and the art filename are keyed off `(setlist, index)` independently. That means a missing catalog still shows art, and missing art still shows the title — neither failure cascades. The CSV is also append-column forward-compatible, so *if* a song ever needs a non-conventional art path we can add an optional `art` column later without breaking anything. I'd not add it now.

**"2 versions (small, large)"** — this is the one thing §4.8.7 doesn't cover yet (it specs a single image; exact dimensions are open Q13). Each distinct size = one fixed-size DDR cache, so the layout should map one size → one walkable group. That's the structural decision worth locking now.

# Song catalog loader (marvin, spec §4.8.3)

## Context

The marvin recognizer identifies a selected GH3 song as a `gp_song_t {setlist, index, tmpl}`
(`game/gameplay_select.h`). The compile-time templates in `game/gameplay_metadata.h` carry only a
machine slug (`song_id`, e.g. `"slow_ride"`) — no human title, artist, BPM, or length. So the UI and
the high-score display can only show `main #4`, not "Slow Ride".

The catalog loader closes that gap: it maps the recognizer's stable `(setlist, index)` key →
human-meaningful labels read from the SD card, so a missing/stale catalog degrades to "Unknown song"
but **never** affects recognition (recognition stays compile-time in flash). It is the next SD
consumer after `storage`/`time`/`results`, and is buildable now — it keys off data that already
exists, with no dependency on the rest of the gameplay engine being resolved.

**Decisions settled with Greg this session:**
- **Format = flat CSV** (`songs.csv`), not the JSON the spec currently names — same rationale that
  moved `results` to CSV (no on-device JSON tokenizer, `FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1`, static buffers; opens in
  pandas/Excel). Spec §4.8.3 gets reconciled to CSV.
- **Stale-version check deferred.** `gameplay_metadata.h` does not emit a `GP_METADATA_VERSION`
  define yet (the generated header would need `export_c.py` to add it). Build the core lookup now;
  the loader degrades to "Unknown song" on any miss regardless. The stale-warning lands later once
  `export_c.py` stamps the version. Tracked as an open item.

## CSV format — `<card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv`

```
setlist,index,title,artist,bpm,length_s
main,0,"Slow Ride","Foghat",0,0
main,4,"Rock and Roll All Nite","Kiss",0,0
bonus,24,"Through the Fire and Flames","DragonForce",0,0
```

- `setlist` is the string `main`/`bonus` (human-editable, matches `results.csv`); mapped to the
  numeric `GP_SETLIST_MAIN`/`GP_SETLIST_BONUS` on load. This same string is the art filename key
  (`main-04`, `bonus-12`), so catalog rows and art files share one `(setlist, index)` identifier.
- `title`/`artist` are CSV-quoted (may contain commas); parsed with the shared quote-aware splitter.
- `bpm`/`length_s` are optional integers (0 = unknown). Rows may be sparse / out of order; only
  `(setlist, index)` need be unique.
- Header row required; the loader skips it. Path is `Storage_MountPoint()`-relative, exactly like
  `results` (`players/results.csv`), so it lands under `games/gh3-wii/` at the card root.

## SD card layout (catalog + future art, locked now)

The catalog and album art are **siblings under `games/<game>/`**, both keyed by `(setlist, index)`
and fully independent of each other (missing catalog still shows art; missing art still shows the
title). Art is **not** referenced from `songs.csv` — firmware derives the art path directly from the
recognizer key, so the catalog needs no art columns.

```
<card>/games/gh3-wii/
  songs.csv                 ← catalog (this change)
  art/                      ← album art (spec §4.8.7; marvin side NOT implemented here)
    small/  main-04.jpg  bonus-12.png   ← one fixed-size DDR cache tier
    large/  main-04.jpg  bonus-12.png   ← one fixed-size DDR cache tier
```

Two artwork sizes use **size-tier subdirs** (`art/small/`, `art/large/`): each subdir maps 1:1 to one
fixed-size pre-decode cache (firmware walks one dir per tier), and a 3rd size is just another subdir.
Filename within is the key (`<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}`, zero-padded index). Exact px per tier is
settled later under Q13. **This change only locks the directory structure (doc-only spec update); no
marvin art loader/cache code lands here.**

#ifndef MARVIN_UTIL_CSV_H
#define MARVIN_UTIL_CSV_H

#include <stddef.h>

/* Minimal CSV field helpers shared by the SD-card consumers (results, catalog).
 * Quote-aware and zero-alloc: csv_split rewrites the line in place and stores
 * pointers into it, csv_quote writes into a caller buffer. Fits the
 * static-allocation rule and FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1 (one line at a time). */

/* Write s into out as a quoted CSV field ("..."), doubling any embedded quote.
 * Always quoted, so embedded commas are safe. Truncates to fit. */
void csv_quote(const char *s, char *out, size_t n);

/* Split a CSV line in place into fields[], honoring double-quoted fields
 * (commas inside quotes, "" -> "). Returns the field count. */
int csv_split(char *line, char *fields[], int maxf);

#endif

```

#include "util/csv.h"

void csv_quote(const char *s, char *out, size_t n)
{
    size_t j = 0;
    if (n == 0) { return; }
    if (s == NULL) { s = ""; }

    if (j < n - 1) { out[j++] = '"'; }
    for (size_t i = 0; s[i] != '\0' && j < n - 2; i++)
    {
        if (s[i] == '"' && j < n - 3) { out[j++] = '"'; }   /* escape by doubling */
        out[j++] = s[i];
    }
    if (j < n - 1) { out[j++] = '"'; }
    out[j] = '\0';
}

int csv_split(char *line, char *fields[], int maxf)
{
    int nf = 0;
    char *p = line;

    while (nf < maxf)
    {
        if (*p == '"')
        {
            p++;
            char *w = p;            /* unescape in place */
            fields[nf++] = w;
            while (*p != '\0')
            {
                if (*p == '"')
                {
                    if (p[1] == '"') { *w++ = '"'; p += 2; }
                    else { p++; break; }   /* closing quote */
                }
                else { *w++ = *p++; }
            }
            *w = '\0';
            while (*p != '\0' && *p != ',' && *p != '\n' && *p != '\r') { p++; }
        }
        else
        {
            fields[nf++] = p;
            while (*p != '\0' && *p != ',' && *p != '\n' && *p != '\r') { p++; }
        }

        if (*p == ',') { *p = '\0'; p++; }
        else { *p = '\0'; break; }
    }
    return nf;
}

```

#ifndef MARVIN_GAME_CATALOG_H
#define MARVIN_GAME_CATALOG_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "game/gameplay_select.h"   /* gp_song_t */

/* Song catalog: maps the recognizer's stable (setlist, index) key to human
 * labels (title/artist/bpm/length) read from <card>/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv
 * (spec §4.8.3). Labels only — recognition stays compile-time in flash, so a
 * missing/stale catalog degrades to "Unknown song" and never affects play.
 *
 * Flat CSV (header + one row per song), parsed with the shared quote-aware
 * splitter (util/csv.h) into a static cache on first use; no malloc, fits
 * FF_FS_MAX_FILES=1 since the file is closed once loaded. Editable on a PC in
 * pandas/Excel, like results.csv. */

typedef struct
{
    uint8_t  setlist;     /* GP_SETLIST_* */
    uint8_t  index;       /* song ordinal within its setlist */
    char     title[64];
    char     artist[48];
    uint16_t bpm;         /* 0 = unknown */
    uint16_t length_s;    /* 0 = unknown */
} catalog_entry_t;

void Catalog_Initialize(void);   /* state only; no I/O (call before scheduler) */

/* Look up one song's labels. Lazy-loads the catalog from the card on first call
 * (and after a failed load, retries only on an explicit Catalog_Reload). Returns
 * true and fills *out on a hit; false on miss / empty catalog (caller shows
 * "Unknown song"). */
bool Catalog_Lookup(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index, catalog_entry_t *out);

/* Convenience wrapper keyed by a recognizer result. */
bool Catalog_LookupSong(const gp_song_t *song, catalog_entry_t *out);

/* Force a fresh read from the card (e.g. after a card swap). Returns true if the
 * catalog file was read (even with zero rows); false on mount/open failure. */
bool Catalog_Reload(void);

int  Catalog_Count(void);     /* entries currently cached */
bool Catalog_IsLoaded(void);  /* a load has been attempted */

/* Direct access to a cached entry by position [0, Catalog_Count()), or NULL.
 * For the `catalog ls` console listing; pointer is valid until the next reload. */
const catalog_entry_t *Catalog_At(int i);

#endif

```

#include "game/catalog.h"

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"

#include "storage/storage.h"
#include "util/csv.h"
#include "game/gameplay_metadata.h"   /* GP_SETLIST_*, GP_N_SONGS */

#define CAT_REL_FILE  "games/gh3-wii/songs.csv"
#define CAT_LINE_MAX  256
#define CAT_FIELDS    6   /* setlist,index,title,artist,bpm,length_s */

static catalog_entry_t s_entries[GP_N_SONGS];
static int             s_count  = 0;
static bool            s_loaded = false;

/* ---- helpers ------------------------------------------------------------ */

static void build_path(char *buf, size_t n, const char *rel)
{
    (void)snprintf(buf, n, "%s/%s", Storage_MountPoint(), rel);
}

/* "main"/"bonus" -> GP_SETLIST_*, or -1 for an unrecognized setlist. */
static int setlist_id(const char *s)
{
    if (strcmp(s, "main")  == 0) { return GP_SETLIST_MAIN; }
    if (strcmp(s, "bonus") == 0) { return GP_SETLIST_BONUS; }
    return -1;
}

static void copy_field(char *dst, size_t n, const char *src)
{
    strncpy(dst, src, n - 1);
    dst[n - 1] = '\0';
}

/* ---- load --------------------------------------------------------------- */

void Catalog_Initialize(void)
{
    s_count  = 0;
    s_loaded = false;
}

bool Catalog_Reload(void)
{
    s_count  = 0;
    s_loaded = true;   /* one attempt; lookups won't re-load until next Reload */

    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return false; }

    char path[80];
    build_path(path, sizeof(path), CAT_REL_FILE);

    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID) { return false; }

    bool first = true;
    char line[CAT_LINE_MAX];

    while (!SYS_FS_FileEOF(h) && s_count < GP_N_SONGS)
    {
        if (SYS_FS_FileStringGet(h, line, sizeof(line)) != SYS_FS_RES_SUCCESS) { break; }
        if (first) { first = false; continue; }   /* header row */
        if (line[0] == '\0' || line[0] == '\n' || line[0] == '\r') { continue; }

        char *f[CAT_FIELDS];
        if (csv_split(line, f, CAT_FIELDS) < CAT_FIELDS) { continue; }

        int sl = setlist_id(f[0]);
        if (sl < 0) { continue; }

        catalog_entry_t *e = &s_entries[s_count];
        e->setlist  = (uint8_t)sl;
        e->index    = (uint8_t)atoi(f[1]);
        copy_field(e->title,  sizeof(e->title),  f[2]);
        copy_field(e->artist, sizeof(e->artist), f[3]);
        e->bpm      = (uint16_t)strtoul(f[4], NULL, 10);
        e->length_s = (uint16_t)strtoul(f[5], NULL, 10);
        s_count++;
    }

    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
    LOG_INFO("CAT: loaded %d song(s)\r\n", s_count);
    return true;
}

/* ---- lookup ------------------------------------------------------------- */

bool Catalog_Lookup(uint8_t setlist, uint8_t index, catalog_entry_t *out)
{
    if (out == NULL) { return false; }
    if (!s_loaded) { (void)Catalog_Reload(); }

    for (int i = 0; i < s_count; i++)
    {
        if (s_entries[i].setlist == setlist && s_entries[i].index == index)
        {
            *out = s_entries[i];
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

bool Catalog_LookupSong(const gp_song_t *song, catalog_entry_t *out)
{
    if (song == NULL) { return false; }
    return Catalog_Lookup(song->setlist, song->index, out);
}

int  Catalog_Count(void)    { return s_count; }
bool Catalog_IsLoaded(void) { return s_loaded; }

const catalog_entry_t *Catalog_At(int i)
{
    if (i < 0 || i >= s_count) { return NULL; }
    return &s_entries[i];
}

```

```md
# marvin SD-card data (seed)

Files here mirror the FAT32 layout marvin expects on the SD card. Copy the tree
to the card root. Paths are relative to the mount point (spec §4.6.2, §4.8).

\```
games/gh3-wii/
  songs.csv          song catalog — labels keyed by (setlist, index); spec §4.8.3
  art/               album art, keyed by the same (setlist, index); spec §4.8.7
    small/  <setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     e.g. main-04.jpg   (one DDR cache tier)
    large/  <setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     e.g. bonus-12.png  (one DDR cache tier)
players/
  results.csv        per-player high scores (written by marvin); spec §4.8.6
\```

`songs.csv` columns: `setlist,index,title,artist,bpm,length_s`. `setlist` is
`main`/`bonus`; `title`/`artist` are CSV-quoted; `bpm`/`length_s` are `0` when
unknown. Rows may be sparse or out of order — only `(setlist, index)` is the key.

The catalog is **labels only**: recognition is compile-time in flash, so a
missing or partial `songs.csv` just shows "Unknown song" and never affects play.
Album art is derived directly from `(setlist, index)` and is **not** referenced
from `songs.csv` — the two are independent.

> **The checked-in `songs.csv` is a placeholder seed** generated from the
> recognizer's song slugs (titles auto-humanized; `artist`/`bpm`/`length_s`
> blank). Replace the values with real metadata before relying on the display.

```

```text
455	
456	**Storage split (decided).** The line is drawn by *what the data is coupled to*, not by convenience:
457	
458	- **Compile-time, in flash:** recognizer templates/signatures (centroids, menu baselines, song bitmap templates, thresholds) **and** the menu graph. These are *algorithm-coupled* — a template is only valid paired with the exact grid geometry, sampling, and normalization compiled into the C recognizer, and is re-learned in lockstep when the algorithm changes. They are generated from the host corpus by `tools/gameplay/gameplay/export_c.py` into `gameplay_metadata.h` and consumed through pointers by `gameplay_classify.c` / `gameplay_select.c`. **Recognition never reads the SD card** — so a missing or stale card can never cause a silent misclassification.
459	- **On the SD card (`/marvin/games/<game>/songs.json`):** the song catalog *labels* — the human-meaningful, user-editable metadata that changes independently of the firmware. Keyed by the stable `(setlist, index)` identifier the recognizer already emits (`gp_song_t`):
460	
461	```json
462	{
463	  "game": "gh3-wii",
464	  "metadata_version": "<stamp matching the firmware build>",
465	  "songs": [
466	    { "setlist": "main", "index": 4, "title": "...", "artist": "...", "bpm": 120, "length_s": 210 }
467	  ]
468	}
469	```
470	
471	The catalog is *labels only* — recognition does not depend on it; a missing/stale catalog degrades to "Unknown song", never a functional break. `export_c.py` also emits a `metadata_version` `#define` into `gameplay_metadata.h`; the same value goes in `songs.json` so the UI can warn if the catalog predates a template-set regeneration. Because the catalog is keyed by `(setlist, index)`, a mismatch degrades gracefully rather than misclassifying.
472
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 17:08:38Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>

```text
536	
537	```
538	art/<setlist>-<NN>.{jpg,png}     // e.g. art/main-04.jpg, art/bonus-12.png  (NN = zero-padded index)
539	```
540	
541	**Pre-cache at startup, not per-use.** After the FAT mount (M4), the firmware walks `art/` and decodes every image **once** into a static, pre-allocated cache of fixed-size slots in DDR; runtime artwork access is then an O(1) pointer into RAM — no card I/O, no decode, and no allocation at use time (consistent with the static-allocation rule). A missing/oversized/corrupt file leaves its slot empty → UI placeholder.
542	
543	- **Decoder — Legato's own runtime decoders; no new library.** JPEG (built-in) and PNG (lodepng) are already enabled in this project (`legato_config.h`: `LE_ENABLE_JPEG_DECODER=1`, `LE_ENABLE_PNG_DECODER=1`). Because `LE_STREAMING_ENABLED=0`, the flow is: read the whole compressed file into a RAM buffer → point a `leImage` (`LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_JPEG` / `_PNG`) at it → decode into the cache slot via the Legato image API. Source images authored at the target WxH decode 1:1 (no scaling).
544	- **Cache pixel format & size.** A decoded Legato raster; **RGBA8888** is the natural full-color choice, **RGB_565** (already used by the project's other assets) halves the RAM cost if alpha isn't needed. Cache = `N_songs × W × H × bytes/px`; for ~70 songs at RGBA8888 that's ≈ 4.5 MB (128×128) / 11 MB (200×200) / 18 MB (256×256), all comfortable in the SAM9X75D2G's DDR (framebuffers use only a few MB). On-card JPEGs total ≈ 1.5–3 MB.
545	- **Exact target dimensions + cache pixel format** are settled when the Legato artwork UI slot is designed. Tracked as Q13.
546	
547	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
548	
549	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
550	
551	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). The console is instead a small in-tree module (`console/console.{h,c}`) in the same shape as `fretboard_link`/`perf_log`: it owns the USART plib directly, is fully statically allocated, and is kept out of MCC via `user.cmake`.
```
</details></tool-use>

Short answer: **yes, both work fine.** In CSV, only three characters are actually "special" — comma, double-quote (`"`), and newline. Apostrophe (`'`) and ampersand (`&`) are ordinary bytes that pass straight through both the file and the on-device `csv_split` parser.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 17:24:25Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 17:24:30Z)**_

Confirmed against the actual parser. The rules, concretely:

| Character | Special in CSV? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `'` apostrophe — *School's Out* | No | Type it as-is. Quotes optional. |
| `&` ampersand — *3's & 7's* | No | Type it as-is. |
| `,` comma — *Lewis, Leona* | **Yes** | Wrap the field in `"…"` (the seed already quotes title/artist, so you're covered). |
| `"` double-quote — *He said "hi"* | **Yes** | Double it: `""` inside a quoted field. |

So your edited rows just look like:

```
main,6,"School's Out","Alice Cooper",0,0
main,32,"3's & 7's","Beck",0,0
```

Two caveats unrelated to the special-character question:

1. **Length** — `title[64]` / `artist[48]` in `catalog_entry_t`. Anything longer is truncated on load (not a parse error). GH3 titles fit comfortably.
2. **Non-ASCII / accents** — e.g. *Mauvais Garçon* (`ç`). The parser is byte-oriented, so UTF-8 passes through cleanly into the buffer; whether the accented glyph *renders* depends on the Legato UI font later. Not a CSV issue — just keep it in mind when the artwork/UI screen is built.

The checked-in seed has the auto-humanized placeholders (`School S Out`, `3 S 7 S`) precisely so you can replace them with the real punctuated titles — that's the intended workflow.

=== metadata.py ===
"""Per-screen menu metadata — the seed of the spec §4.8.3 menu tables.

For each static-list screen the navigator needs to act on, this records the
ordered item list (ids = the corpus filename suffixes, matching the index order
in `gh3_navigation.md`) and the on-screen geometry of the menu: a bounding band
plus the axis the items run along. The highlight reader divides the band into
`len(items)` equal cells and finds the lit one.

Scope today: fixed-item-count static lists. Deferred:
- `section_select` — item count is song-dependent (navigator just saturates to the
  top "FULL SONG"); doesn't fit a fixed-row-index model.
- `song_select` — fixed-slot/scrolling; "reading" the selected song is nearest-
  bitmap matching of the highlight slot against the known per-song templates, a
  separate concern from row reading (and distinct from char-level OCR, which is
  only needed later for open-ended values like scores).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

VERTICAL = "v"
HORIZONTAL = "h"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MenuLayout:
    screen_id: str
    items: tuple[str, ...]  # item ids (= filename suffixes) in screen order (top->bottom / left->right)
    band: tuple[int, int, int, int]  # (x0, y0, x1, y1) in canonical 720x480 space
    axis: str = VERTICAL

    @property
    def count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.items)

    def index_of(self, item_id: str) -> int:
        return self.items.index(item_id)


# Bands are in canonical 720x480 space, converged against the labelled corpus by
# auto-locating each selection's highlight (see docs/journal.md). `items` is in
# screen order (top->bottom, or left->right for horizontal), which is what the
# reader maps cells onto.
MENU_LAYOUTS: dict[str, MenuLayout] = {
    "main_menu": MenuLayout(
        "main_menu",
        ("career", "co_op_career", "quickplay", "multiplayer", "training", "options", "nintendo_wfc"),

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 17:47:38Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 17:47:48Z)**_

The accent bytes (`C3 A9` = é, `C3 A7` = ç) pass through `csv_split` and the `strncpy` into the cache buffer completely intact. Here's the full chain and why it's safe:

| Stage | UTF-8 behavior |
|---|---|
| **FatFs file read** (`SYS_FS_FileStringGet`) | Byte-oriented (fgets-style); stops only at `\n`. File *contents* are opaque bytes — FatFs never transcodes them. |
| **`csv_split` / `csv_quote`** | Only ever test for ASCII `"` `,` `\n` `\r`. UTF-8 guarantees no multibyte sequence contains a byte < 0x80, so accent bytes can never collide with a delimiter. Copied verbatim. |
| **`catalog_entry_t` cache** | `char title[64]` / `artist[48]` — raw bytes via `strncpy`. Proven above. |
| **Console `catalog ls`** | Emits the bytes verbatim over UART; renders correctly in any UTF-8 terminal. |
| **Legato** | Receives the UTF-8 byte string; renders per the font (your part). |

So nothing in marvin's path needs to "support" UTF-8 — it's transparent because it never interprets the high bytes. Use real glyphs in `songs.csv` whenever you like; the ASCII spellings in the seed were only for consistency with `fetch_gh3_cover_art.py`, not a limitation.

Three caveats worth knowing:

1. **Buffers count bytes, not characters** — `title[64]` holds ~64 ASCII chars but fewer accented ones (é = 2 bytes). Fine for these titles; just the real ceiling.
2. **Truncation isn't UTF-8-aware** — if a title ever exceeds the buffer, `strncpy` can clip mid-sequence and leave one dangling byte (a single mojibake glyph at the end). Only bites very long accented titles. If you want, I can make `copy_field` back off to the last complete codepoint on truncation — a few lines.
3. **Filenames are the one place encoding config matters** — file *contents* are always opaque, but FatFs long-filename handling depends on `FF_CODE_PAGE`/`FF_LFN`. Irrelevant for `songs.csv` (ASCII), but if you ever name an art file with accents, that's the setting to check. The catalog/art design avoids this by keying filenames off `(setlist, index)` — pure ASCII.

Want me to switch the seed to accented forms (and update `fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` in lockstep so they stay keyed to the same data), and/or add the UTF-8-aware truncation guard?

## On the BOM question

You're remembering the **UTF-8 BOM** — an optional 3-byte signature `EF BB BF` at the very start of the file. I checked: this file has **none** (first bytes are `73 65 74` = `set…`, the header). That's deliberate.

The key thing: **UTF-8 is not "tagged" anywhere.** A text file carries no encoding metadata — encoding is pure convention. The BOM is the *only* in-band hint, and it's:

- **Meaningful for UTF-16/UTF-32** — there it signals byte order (endianness), which is genuinely ambiguous.
- **Optional and discouraged for UTF-8** — UTF-8 is a byte sequence with no byte-order ambiguity, so the BOM is just a "this is UTF-8" marker that mainly older Windows apps (Notepad, some Excel versions) write/expect.

I'd keep it **BOM-less** because:
1. It's the Unix/embedded standard; a BOM trips up `awk`, `grep`, `diff`, and naive line parsers (the leading column name becomes `\xEF\xBB\xBFsetlist`).
2. Our on-device loader doesn't need it and is **immune either way** — it unconditionally skips the first line as the header, so even if you edit-and-save in Excel-on-Windows and it injects a BOM, those 3 bytes land on the discarded header line and never reach a data row. (Just don't let a BOM end up mid-file — which won't happen from normal editing.)

So: not tagged, no BOM, plain UTF-8 — and the system reads it correctly regardless.

One thing I did **not** touch: I noticed the source table lists The Fall of Troy's album as `Doppelganger` — the real title is *Doppelgänger* (ä). It's an **album** field, which the catalog CSV doesn't use, so I left it alone. Want me to fix that one too for the cover-art fetcher's accuracy?

Good instinct to think about this now — adding columns later is *mostly* safe (our reader ignores extra trailing columns, so an old firmware reads a new card fine), but a new firmware reading an old card degrades to "Unknown," and since the seed + loader are co-versioned here with no cards deployed yet, now's the cheap moment to settle the schema.

Two realities shape the answer:

1. **Cost is trivial** — each field is a few bytes × 64 entries in DDR (we have MBs). Not a constraint.
2. **Data is the real work** — I have title/artist/album from the in-repo table. I do **not** have reliable year/genre/difficulty for 64 songs and won't fabricate them. So "add the column" and "fill it correctly" are separate steps.

How I'd triage the candidates:

| Field | Verdict | Why / data source |
|---|---|---|
| **year** | **Add** | Cheap, useful for display, and *sourceable* — `fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` already hits MusicBrainz; the release-group has a first-release-date, so I can populate it in the same pass as cover art. |
| **GH3 difficulty rating** (the in-game flame tier, 1–6) | **Add** | The spec literally anticipated this ("expected difficulty score"). It's the most *marvin-relevant* field — sets play expectations, could gate auto-play. Fixed per song; data is manual (GH3 wiki). |
| **genre** | Optional | Display/filter only, and fuzzy (MB tags are noisy). Fine to carry an empty slot, but lower value. |
| tier name, playable parts, note count, decade | Skip | Derivable (decade←year, main/bonus←setlist) or low-value bloat. |

My recommendation: **add `year` + `difficulty` now, `genre` only if you want the slot.** I'd append them after `length_s` (keeps the safe-append property), leave `difficulty`/`genre` blank for now, and wire `year` into the MB fetch so it fills automatically.

```text
MB_ROOT = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2"
CAA_ROOT = "https://coverartarchive.org"

_last_mb_call = [0.0]


def mb_get(path, params, user_agent, min_interval=1.1):
    """GET a MusicBrainz endpoint as JSON, throttled to <=1 req/sec."""
    wait = min_interval - (time.time() - _last_mb_call[0])
    if wait > 0:
        time.sleep(wait)
    params = dict(params, fmt="json")
    url = "%s/%s?%s" % (MB_ROOT, path, urllib.parse.urlencode(params))
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": user_agent})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            data = json.load(resp)
    finally:
        _last_mb_call[0] = time.time()
    return data


def lucene_escape(s):
    for ch in r'+-&|!(){}[]^"~*?:\/':
        s = s.replace(ch, "\\" + ch)
    return s


def find_release_groups(artist, album, user_agent):
    """Return candidate release-group MBIDs, best score first."""
    q = 'releasegroup:"%s" AND artist:"%s"' % (lucene_escape(album), lucene_escape(artist))
    data = mb_get("release-group", {"query": q, "limit": 5}, user_agent)
    return [rg["id"] for rg in data.get("release-groups", [])]


def find_releases_via_recording(artist, title, user_agent):
    """Fallback: find releases that carry a recording of <title> by <artist>."""
    q = 'recording:"%s" AND artist:"%s"' % (lucene_escape(title), lucene_escape(artist))
    data = mb_get("recording", {"query": q, "limit": 10}, user_agent)
    ids = []
    for rec in data.get("recordings", []):
        for rel in rec.get("releases", []):
            if rel["id"] not in ids:
                ids.append(rel["id"])
    return ids[:5]


def caa_fetch(kind, mbid, size, user_agent):
    """Download the front cover for a release-group/release. Returns (bytes, ext) or None."""
    suffix = "front-%d" % size if size else "front"
    url = "%s/%s/%s/%s" % (CAA_ROOT, kind, mbid, suffix)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": user_agent})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            blob = resp.read()
            ctype = resp.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if e.code == 404:
            return None
        raise
    ext = "png" if "png" in ctype else "jpg"
    return blob, ext


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--contact", required=True,
                    help="Your email or project URL (required by the MusicBrainz API)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="gh3_cover_art", help="Output directory")
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=500, choices=[250, 500, 1200, 0],
                    help="Cover size in px; 0 = full resolution (default 500)")
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="Re-download even if file exists")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    user_agent = "gh3-coverart/1.0 ( %s )" % args.contact
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)

    hits, misses = 0, []
    for setlist, idx, slug, title, artist, album in SONGS:
        base = "%s_%02d_%s" % (setlist, idx, slug)
        existing = [f for f in os.listdir(args.out) if f.startswith(base + ".")]
        if existing and not args.force:
            print("  skip  %-30s (have %s)" % (base, existing[0]))
            hits += 1
            continue

        print("fetch  %-30s  %s - %s" % (base, artist, album or "(no album)"))
        blob = None
        try:
            # Primary: release-group front cover.
            if album:
                for mbid in find_release_groups(artist, album, user_agent):
                    got = caa_fetch("release-group", mbid, args.size, user_agent)
                    if got:
                        blob = got
                        break
            # Fallback: any release carrying a recording of this song.
            if blob is None:
                for mbid in find_releases_via_recording(artist, title, user_agent):
                    got = caa_fetch("release", mbid, args.size, user_agent)
                    if got:
                        blob = got
                        break
        except Exception as e:  # network hiccup, etc. -- log and continue
```

**Data sourcing (per your choices):**
- **difficulty** → reserved blank column. GH3 has no per-song rating; the authentic signal is career tier, deferred (noted in spec + journal).
- **year + genre** → I extended `tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py` with a `--catalog` mode: it sources the original-release `year` (release-group first-release-date, with a recording fallback) and a `genre` (artist's top MusicBrainz genre/tag) in the same throttled pass, then writes `songs.csv`. Run it with network:
  ```
  python3 tools/fetch_gh3_cover_art.py --contact you@example.com \
      --catalog firmware/marvin/data/games/gh3-wii/songs.csv
  ```
  The MB-enrichment functions can't run in this sandbox (network restricted), but I verified the rest offline: `py_compile` passes, and `--no-enrich` reproduces the committed `songs.csv` **byte-for-byte** — so the writer/quoting are correct and the only untested part is the MB JSON parse, which you'll see reported (`year filled for N`) when you run it.

**Docs:** `data/README.md`, spec §4.8.3, the journal decision entry + focus note, and the `catalog.h` header comment all updated to the 10-column schema and the sourcing story.

Why I didn't just fill the values myself: WebSearch is disabled on my model, the Guitar Hero wiki 403s automated fetches, and Wikipedia only lists a handful — so hand-typing 64 rows of year/genre would've been guesswork. _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 23:09:54Z)**_

That check is decisive. Here's what the repo's Legato setup tells us:

- **`LE_LIST_WIDGET_ENABLED 0`, `LE_LISTWHEEL_WIDGET_ENABLED 0`, `LE_SCROLLBAR_WIDGET_ENABLED 0`** — the built-in list/scroll widgets are turned off. And even if enabled, `leListWidget`'s item model is **icon + a single string** — it can't render your row (color tier badge + bold title + dim artist on a second line + right-aligned duration). So the stock list widget is out on two counts. Your instinct is right.
- The established pattern here is **MGS authors the screen** (`le_gen_screen_Marvin.{h,c}`) and **marvin implements event callbacks in a thin shim** (`ui/manual_input.c` wires the strum buttons). The list should follow that: MGS places an empty container where the list goes; a new `ui/song_list.c` owns the rows + scroll.
- `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_ENABLE 1` (Legato heap) — and the journal already flags watching `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE`. So per-row dynamic widget churn is the thing to avoid.
- Good news: base `leWidget` panels + `Label`/`Image` (enabled) + scheme background fills cover everything in that row — **no new widget enables needed** (highlight = a panel's background fill; badge = a small color-schemed panel + label).

The real fork is how the list paints and scrolls. Three options, ruling one out immediately:

**Rejected — enable `leListWidget`:** least code, but it physically can't do the rich two-line row. Would force a flat single-line list, losing the design.

**A. Virtualized recycled-row list (my recommendation).** A clipped panel viewport (sized/placed in MGS) holds a *fixed pool* of ~`visible+2` composite row widgets (panel + tier-badge + title + artist + duration labels). Created once at screen-show — no per-scroll allocation, so it respects static-allocation and won't churn the Legato heap. Touch-drag translates the content Y; rows scrolling off an edge are recycled to the other end and re-bound from `Catalog_At(i)`. Selection = toggle the row panel's background fill. Inertia is hand-rolled (track drag velocity, decay on a timer). Rich rows come "for free" from Legato labels.

**B. Single custom-painted widget.** One widget paints only the visible rows itself via Legato's draw API (or a `DrawSurface` paint hook) and handles touch. Zero per-row widgets, leanest memory, smoothest virtualization and inertia — but you hand-draw text/badges/clipping and wire up custom paint, giving up MGS for the list interior.

Both are single-finger drag, which matches the existing "single-finger momentary" input decision — no multitouch needed.

Two things this surfaces regardless of approach:
- **Tier data gap.** The `T1/T3` badges and the center `TIER 3 ★★★` need the career-tier we deferred (the reserved-blank `difficulty` column). This screen is the reason to revisit it — likely a real `tier` column.
- **List data model.** "SETLIST · 15 TRACKS" + tier badges looks like a *career setlist grouped by tier*, not the flat 64-song catalog. So there's a setlist/tier model to define on top of `Catalog_At()`. Worth settling before we build the list, since it shapes the row data.

Which way do you want to go on the list itself?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 23:14:31Z)**_

Good question to pin down, because "single custom widget" has two very different meanings and only one of them is sane here.

**The version I'm recommending is still *inside* Legato — on top of it, not outside it.** It's a Legato widget whose *paint* and *touch* handlers you write, but everything else is Legato's:

- it lives in the widget tree as a child of the MGS-authored screen;
- Legato positions/sizes/**clips** it (so rows can't spill past the viewport);
- touch reaches it through the **same input pipeline** as your buttons (`leWidget` touch-down/moved/up handlers) — no separate touch path;
- it paints with **Legato's renderer** into Legato's layer/scratch buffer, and participates in Legato's **dirty-rect / refresh** cycle (you call invalidate; Legato schedules the repaint);
- crucially, "hand-draw text" means you call Legato's **draw-string with x/y positions using the MGS-generated fonts** — you are *not* writing a glyph rasterizer. Same fonts as the rest of the screen.

So vs. approach A, the integration level is identical. The only difference is A composes child `Label` widgets per row, while B is one widget that draws primitives in its paint callback. Both are Legato citizens.

Two ways to get that paint hook, FYI:
- **`leDrawSurfaceWidget`** — the supported "here's a canvas in the tree, draw into it" widget (a paint/draw callback). Currently disabled in `legato_config.h`; enabling is an MGS toggle.
- **Subclass `leWidget`** — copy the vtable, override `paint` + the touch handlers. More boilerplate, no DrawSurface dependency.

**The genuinely "outside Legato" path** does exist, since we own the BGRX32 framebuffer and the XLCDC OVR1 layer: you could blit rows straight into the DDR buffer with your own code and read the maxtouch driver directly. But inside a Legato screen that's a bad mix — Legato assumes it owns its layer and manages clip/dirty/refresh, so raw draws behind its back get overpainted or tear. It'd only make sense if the *whole* UI were non-Legato, which it isn't. So: don't.

Net: pick A or B for *how much you lean on Legato's widget model*, but either way you're building **with** Legato, not around it.

A couple of things that might help you think it through:
- **Memory:** A allocates ~`(visible+2)×~4` widgets once from the Legato heap at screen-show (bounded, no churn). B allocates **one** widget — lightest, and the clearest win against the `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` worry.
- **Effort split:** A is less Legato-internals work (labels do layout/text), more bookkeeping (recycle pool, rebind on scroll). B is more upfront paint/touch plumbing, then dead simple to extend (add a column = one more draw call).
- **The non-list dependencies don't change with this choice** — you still need the tier data (deferred column) and the setlist/tier data model either way.

Happy to go deeper on any of these — e.g. sketch what the B paint callback + touch/inertia actually looks like, or how the recycle pool in A works — whatever helps you decide.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 23:20:19Z)**_

Confirmed against the copy vendored in this repo — Legato gives you everything; **no library edits needed.** Two public extension points are both present:

1. **DrawSurface widget** — `leDrawSurfaceWidget` with a public `leDrawSurfaceWidget_DrawCallback` + `setDrawCallback` ([legato_widget_drawsurface.h:73,93](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/drawsurface/legato_widget_drawsurface.h)). That's a ready-made "canvas in the widget tree, here's your paint callback." The source is already vendored; it's just gated off by `LE_DRAWSURFACE_WIDGET_ENABLED 0`.

2. **Subclass `leWidget`** — `leWidgetVTable` and the per-widget `const leWidgetVTable* fn` pointer are public ([legato_widget.h:562,626](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h)), as are `leWidget_New()` / `leWidget_Constructor()` and the touch-event vtable slots. So you allocate your own struct, point its vtable at your `paint`/touch overrides, and it behaves like any built-in widget.

Either path, the paint body calls Legato's **renderer** (`leRenderer_*` clip/draw, the string/rect draws) into Legato's own layer — same machinery the stock widgets use.

So your custom widget lives entirely in **our** module (`ui/song_list.c`, added via `user.cmake`) using public Legato headers — **zero edits to the generated `gfx/legato/` tree**, which is exactly the discipline this project follows (hand code stays out of regenerated trees; no re-apply patches).

One nuance worth knowing as you weigh them:
- **DrawSurface** is the lower-effort hook, but enabling it flips `LE_DRAWSURFACE_WIDGET_ENABLED` in the generated `legato_config.h` — so do that **through MGS** (a checkbox), not a hand-edit, so it survives the next regen.
- **`leWidget` subclass** needs **no config change at all** — the base widget is always compiled. Slightly more boilerplate (vtable setup), but nothing to toggle and nothing that can get clobbered.

And yes — agreed on the mockup: the real screen binds rows and the detail panel from the catalog (`Catalog_At` / `Catalog_Lookup`); the JPEG's specific songs/tiers are just placeholder art.

No decision needed now. When you want to go deeper, good next things to chew on: DrawSurface-toggle vs subclass (config-surface tradeoff above), and the **setlist/tier data model** (the `T1/T3` grouping implies a tier field we deferred) — that shapes the row data regardless of which paint path you pick.

void Legato_Tasks(void)  // FreeRTOS task at 10ms interval (line 120)
{
    switch(legatoState) {
        case LEGATO_STATE_INIT: { /* ... */ break; }
        case LEGATO_STATE_RUNNING:
        {
            legato_updateScreenState();  // Calls screenShow_Marvin() if screen changed
            leUpdate(0);                 // This is THE MAIN UPDATE CALL
            break;
        }
    }
}
```

**FreeRTOS task definition (from `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/tasks.c`, lines 115-122):**
```c

{
    while(1)
    {
        Legato_Tasks();
        vTaskDelay(10 / portTICK_PERIOD_MS);  // 10 ms tick rate
    }
}
```

**`screenUpdate_Marvin()` called every frame (from `le_gen_init.c`, lines 82-95):**

**For inertia animation, use the widget's `update()` vtable entry:**

When you create your custom scrolling widget, override its `update()` method:
```c
// In your custom widget implementation:
void CustomScrollList_Update(leWidget* _this, uint32_t dt)
{
    CustomScrollList* widget = (CustomScrollList*)_this;
    
    // dt is milliseconds since last call
    // Apply inertia decay:
    if(widget->velocityY != 0) {
        widget->offsetY += widget->velocityY * dt / 1000.0f;  // dt in ms
        widget->velocityY *= 0.95f;  // friction decay
        
        // Clamp to bounds
        if(widget->velocityY < 1 && widget->velocityY > -1) {
            widget->velocityY = 0;
        }
        
        widget->fn->invalidate(widget);  // Mark for redraw
    }
}
```

The `leUpdate()` call at the top level propagates down to every widget's `update()` method. From the widget vtable definition (`legato_widget.h`):
```c
void (*update)(THIS_TYPE* _this, uint32_t dt);  // Called every frame
```

**Summary of the timing:**
- `Legato_Tasks()` runs every 10 ms in FreeRTOS
- Each call to `Legato_Tasks()` calls `leUpdate(0)` 
- `leUpdate()` walks the widget tree and calls each widget's `update(dt)` method
- Your custom widget's `update()` is the hook for scroll inertia

### (d) Screen Switching Mechanism

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.c`

**How screens are shown:**
```c
void legato_initializeScreenState(void)  // Called at startup
{
    screenInit_Screen0();
    screenInit_Marvin();
    legato_showScreen(screenID_Marvin);  // Show Marvin initially
}

void legato_showScreen(uint32_t id)
{
    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
        return;
    changingToScreen = id;  // Flag change (doesn't happen immediately)
}

void legato_updateScreenState(void)  // Called every frame
{
    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_TRUE)
        return;  // Can't change mid-render
    
    if(changingToScreen >= 0) {
        legato_hideCurrentScreen();
        leEvent_ClearList();
        
        switch(changingToScreen) {
            case screenID_Marvin:
                screenShow_Marvin();  // Creates all widgets
                break;
        }
        
        currentScreen = changingToScreen;
        changingToScreen = -1;
    }
    
    // Every frame, call the active screen's update
    switch(currentScreen) {
        case screenID_Marvin:
            screenUpdate_Marvin();  // 10ms tick
            break;
    }
}
```

## Vendored Legato Graphics Library - Public Widget API Report

This report documents the exact public APIs available in the vendored Legato library at `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato`, extracted from the marvin firmware configuration.

### 1. Widget Base + VTable

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h`

**leWidget struct (lines 624–650):**
```c
typedef struct leWidget
{
    const leWidgetVTable* fn;      // vtable pointer
    
    uint32_t id;                    // widget id
    leWidgetType type;              // widget type enum
    
    leRect rect;                    // bounding rectangle (x, y, width, height)
    
    uint32_t flags;                 // state flags (LE_WIDGET_ENABLED, LE_WIDGET_VISIBLE, etc.)
    leWidgetStyle style;            // background type, border type, alignment, alpha, corner radius
    leWidgetStatus status;          // dirty state, draw state
    
    leMargin margin;                // left, top, right, bottom margins
    
    uint32_t drawCount;             // frame counter
    leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr drawFunc;  // current draw function pointer
    
    const leScheme* scheme;         // color scheme reference
    
    leWidgetEventFilter eventFilters[LE_WIDGET_MAX_EVENT_FILTERS];  // event filters
    
    leWidget* parent;               // parent widget
    leArray children;               // child widget array
} leWidget;
```

**leWidgetVTable (lines 562–565):**
The vtable is defined via macro `LE_WIDGET_VTABLE(leWidget)` and includes all position/size getters/setters, visibility, alpha, focus, and crucially:
- `void (*_paint)(THIS_TYPE* _this)` — custom paint function
- `void (*invalidate)(const THIS_TYPE* _this)` — mark dirty
- `void (*_damageArea)(const THIS_TYPE* _this, leRect* rect)` — damage screen region
- `void (*update)(THIS_TYPE* _this, uint32_t dt)` — update/task function
- Touch handlers: `void (*touchDownEvent)`, `(*touchUpEvent)`, `(*touchMoveEvent)`
- Move/resize/focus events

**Creation (lines 688, 700):**
```c
leWidget* leWidget_New(void);                    // allocate from context heap
void leWidget_Constructor(leWidget* wgt);        // init base widget struct
```

**Widget Size Allocation:**
There is **no explicit size parameter**. Each widget type is allocated as its exact struct size (e.g., `sizeof(leButtonWidget)`). The Legato pool allocator (`LE_MALLOC`) handles this:

```c
// From button widget constructor (legato_widget_button.c, line 138):
leButtonWidget* wgt = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leButtonWidget));
leButtonWidget_Constructor(wgt);
```

**Subclass Construction Pattern (from button widget):**

File: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c` (lines 103–146)

```c
// 1. Call base class constructor
void leButtonWidget_Constructor(leButtonWidget* _this)
{
    leWidget_Constructor((leWidget*)_this);     // Initialize base
    
    // 2. Set derived vtable pointers (both base and derived)
    _this->widget.fn = (void*)&buttonWidgetVTable;
    _this->fn = &buttonWidgetVTable;            // Cast-able vtable
    
    // 3. Set widget type
    _this->widget.type = LE_WIDGET_BUTTON;
    
    // 4. Initialize dimensions
    _this->widget.rect.width = DEFAULT_WIDTH;
    _this->widget.rect.height = DEFAULT_HEIGHT;
    
    // 5. Set default style/state
    _this->widget.style.borderType = LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL;
    
    // 6. Initialize custom fields
    _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
    _this->toggleable = LE_FALSE;
    _this->string = NULL;
    // ... other fields
}

// Allocate and construct
leButtonWidget* leButtonWidget_New()
{
    leButtonWidget* wgt = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leButtonWidget));
    if(wgt == NULL)
        return NULL;
    leButtonWidget_Constructor(wgt);
    return wgt;
}

} leWidgetEvent_TouchUp;

typedef struct leWidgetEvent_TouchMove
{

    uint32_t touchID;
    int32_t prevX;            // previous x
    int32_t prevY;            // previous y

} leWidgetEvent_TouchMove;

**VTable Touch Handlers (legato_widget.h, lines 547–549):**

**Touch Capture:**
There is **no explicit "touch capture" API** in this version. Touch is routed to the widget at the touch point. To implement drag/scroll:
- Track `touchID` across down → move → up events
- Use `prevX/prevY` vs current `x/y` to calculate deltas
- Store captured `touchID` in widget state to recognize subsequent moves from the same touch source

```c
static void drawString(leLabelWidget* lbl)
{
    leRect boundingRect = leRect_Zero;
    leRect kerningRect = leRect_Zero;
    leStringRenderRequest req;

    // Get text layout
    _leLabelWidget_GetTextRects(lbl, &boundingRect, &kerningRect);

    // Fill render request
    req.str = lbl->string;
    req.x = kerningRect.x;
    req.y = kerningRect.y;
    req.align = lbl->widget.style.halign;
    req.color = leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT);
    req.alpha = paintState.alpha;  // cumulative alpha
    req.lookupTable = leUtils_GetSchemeLookupTable(
        lbl->widget.scheme,
        req.color,
        leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE));

    // Draw
    leStringRenderer_DrawString(&req);
}

void _leLabelWidget_Paint(leLabelWidget* lbl)
{
    // State machine: draw background → draw string → draw border
    while(lbl->widget.status.drawState != DONE) {
        lbl->widget.drawFunc((leWidget*)lbl);
    }
}
```
