### Summary: Custom Scrollable List Widget Pattern

To build your custom scrollable list:

1. **Define struct** combining base + your fields:
   ```c
   typedef struct leScrollableListWidget {
       leWidget widget;
       const leScrollableListWidgetVTable* fn;
       // Your fields: item array, scroll offset, selection, etc.
   } leScrollableListWidget;
   ```

2. **Allocate & construct**:
   ```c
   leScrollableListWidget* list = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leScrollableListWidget));
   leWidget_Constructor((leWidget*)list);
   list->widget.fn = &vtable;
   list->fn = &vtable;
   list->widget.type = LE_WIDGET_CUSTOM;  // or custom enum
   ```

3. **Touch handling** (in `touchMoveEvent` vtable handler):
   - Track `touchID`, measure delta from `prevX/prevY` to `x/y`
   - Update `scroll_offset` based on delta
   - Call `list->fn->_damageArea(list, &list->widget.rect)` to trigger repaint

4. **Paint function** (vtable `_paint`):
   - Calculate visible item rects (clip to widget bounds)
   - For each visible item, call `leStringRenderer_DrawString()` with item text + font from scheme
   - Use `leScheme_GetRenderColor(widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT)` for text color

5. **Invalidate**:
   - When data changes: `widget.fn->invalidate(widget)`
   - Dirty rect for partial updates: `widget.fn->_damageArea(widget, &changedRect)`

All drawing clipping is automatic; child widgets' rects are clipped to parent bounds during render.

197	        leBackgroundType
198	
199	    Summary:
200	        Specifies the different background types used for the widgets in the library
201	
202	    Description:
203	        Specifies the different background types used for the widgets in the library
204	
205	        None - No background fill.  Widget must defer to its parent to erase dirty
206	               pixels.  This may cause additional overhead as clean pixels may be
207	               repainted as well.
208	
209	        Fill - a scheme color is used to fill the widget rectangle.
210	
211	        Cache - a local framebuffer cache is maintained by the widget and used to
212	                clean up dirty pixels.  Will not cause a parent repaint event but
213	                will use additional memory to contain the cache.
214	
215	    Remarks:
216	        None.
217	 */

39	static LegatoState legatoState;
40	
41	void Legato_Initialize(void)
42	{
43	
44	    gfxIOCTLArg_Palette pal;
45	
46	    leInitialize(&gfxDriverInterface, &gfxGPUInterface);
47	
48	    pal.palette = leGlobalPalette.header.address;
49	    pal.mode = (int)leGlobalPalette.colorMode;
50	    pal.colorCount = leGlobalPalette.colorCount;
51	
52	    gfxDriverInterface.ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_SET_PALETTE, &pal);
53	
54	
55	    legato_initializeScreenState();
56	
57	
58	    inputListener.handleTouchDown = &touchDownHandler;
59	    inputListener.handleTouchUp = &touchUpHandler;
60	    inputListener.handleTouchMove = &touchMoveHandler;
61	
62	    legatoState = LEGATO_STATE_INIT;
63	}
64	
65	void Legato_Tasks(void)
66	{
67	    switch(legatoState)
68	    {
69	        case LEGATO_STATE_INIT:
70	        {
71	            SYS_INP_AddListener(&inputListener);
72	
73	            legatoState = LEGATO_STATE_RUNNING;
74	
75	            break;
76	        }
77	        case LEGATO_STATE_RUNNING:
78	        {
79	            //Legato_DemoModeProcessEvents();
80	
81	            legato_updateScreenState();
82	
83	            leUpdate(0);
84	
85	            break;
86	        }
87	
88	        default:
89	        {
90	            break;
91	        }
92	    }
93	}
94	
95	void touchDownHandler(const SYS_INP_TouchStateEvent* const evt)
96	{
97	    leInput_InjectTouchDown(evt->index, evt->x, evt->y);
98	}
99	
100	void touchUpHandler(const SYS_INP_TouchStateEvent* const evt)
101	{
102	    leInput_InjectTouchUp(evt->index, evt->x, evt->y);
103	}
104	
105	void touchMoveHandler(const SYS_INP_TouchMoveEvent* const evt)
106	{
107	    leInput_InjectTouchMoved(evt->index, evt->x, evt->y);
108	}

1	#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.h"
2	
3	static int32_t currentScreen;
4	static int32_t changingToScreen;
5	
6	void legato_initializeScreenState(void)
7	{
8	    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
9	
10	    initializeStrings();
11	
12	    screenInit_Screen0();
13	    screenInit_Marvin();
14	
15	    currentScreen = -1;
16	    changingToScreen = -1;
17	
18	    legato_showScreen(screenID_Marvin);
19	}
20	
21	uint32_t legato_getCurrentScreen(void)
22	{
23	    return currentScreen;
24	}
25	
26	static void legato_hideCurrentScreen(void)
27	{
28	    switch(currentScreen)
29	    {
30	        case screenID_Screen0:
31	        {
32	            screenHide_Screen0();
33	            currentScreen = 0;
34	            break;
35	        }
36	        case screenID_Marvin:
37	        {
38	            screenHide_Marvin();
39	            currentScreen = 0;
40	            break;
41	        }
42	    }
43	}
44	
45	void legato_showScreen(uint32_t id)
46	{
47	    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
48	        return;
49	
50	    changingToScreen = id;
51	}
52	
53	void legato_updateScreenState(void)
54	{
55	    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_TRUE)
56	        return;
57	
58	    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
59	    {
60	        legato_hideCurrentScreen();
61	
62	        leEvent_ClearList();
63	
64	        switch(changingToScreen)
65	        {
66	            case screenID_Screen0:
67	            {
68	                screenShow_Screen0();
69	                break;
70	            }
71	            case screenID_Marvin:
72	            {
73	                screenShow_Marvin();
74	                break;
75	            }
76	        }
77	
78	        currentScreen = changingToScreen;
79	        changingToScreen = -1;
80	    }
81	
82	    switch(currentScreen)
83	    {
84	        case screenID_Screen0:
85	        {
86	            screenUpdate_Screen0();
87	            break;
88	        }
89	        case screenID_Marvin:
90	        {
91	            screenUpdate_Marvin();
92	            break;
93	        }
94	    }
95	}
96	
97	leBool legato_isChangingScreens(void)
98	{
99	    return changingToScreen != -1;
100	}

```text
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Screen0.h"

// screen member widget declarations
static leWidget* root0;

leImageWidget* Screen0_ImageWidget_0;

static leBool initialized = LE_FALSE;
static leBool showing = LE_FALSE;

leResult screenInit_Screen0(void)
{
    if(initialized == LE_TRUE)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    initialized = LE_TRUE;

    return LE_SUCCESS;
}

leResult screenShow_Screen0(void)
{
    if(showing == LE_TRUE)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    // layer 0
    root0 = leWidget_New();
    root0->fn->setSize(root0, LE_DEFAULT_SCREEN_WIDTH, LE_DEFAULT_SCREEN_HEIGHT);
    root0->fn->setBackgroundType(root0, LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE);
    root0->fn->setMargins(root0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
    root0->flags |= LE_WIDGET_IGNOREEVENTS;
    root0->flags |= LE_WIDGET_IGNOREPICK;

    Screen0_ImageWidget_0 = leImageWidget_New();
    Screen0_ImageWidget_0->fn->setPosition(Screen0_ImageWidget_0, 0, 0);
    Screen0_ImageWidget_0->fn->setSize(Screen0_ImageWidget_0, 1280, 800);
    Screen0_ImageWidget_0->fn->setBorderType(Screen0_ImageWidget_0, LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE);
    Screen0_ImageWidget_0->fn->setImage(Screen0_ImageWidget_0, (leImage*)&Marvin);
    root0->fn->addChild(root0, (leWidget*)Screen0_ImageWidget_0);

    leAddRootWidget(root0, 0);
    leSetLayerColorMode(0, LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565);

    showing = LE_TRUE;

    return LE_SUCCESS;
}

void screenUpdate_Screen0(void)
{
    root0->fn->setSize(root0, root0->rect.width, root0->rect.height);
}

void screenHide_Screen0(void)
{

    leRemoveRootWidget(root0, 0);
    leWidget_Delete(root0);
    root0 = NULL;

    Screen0_ImageWidget_0 = NULL;


    showing = LE_FALSE;
}

void screenDestroy_Screen0(void)
{
    if(initialized == LE_FALSE)
        return;

    initialized = LE_FALSE;
}

leWidget* screenGetRoot_Screen0(uint32_t lyrIdx)
{
    if(lyrIdx >= LE_LAYER_COUNT)
        return NULL;

    switch(lyrIdx)
    {
        case 0:
        {
            return root0;
        }
        default:
        {
            return NULL;
        }
    }
}

42	enum
43	{
44	    NOT_STARTED = LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_READY,
45	    DONE = LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE,
46	    DRAW_BACKGROUND,
47	    DRAW_STRING,
48	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
49	    WAIT_STRING,
50	#endif
51	    DRAW_BORDER,
52	};

54	static struct
55	{
56	    uint32_t alpha;
57	} paintState;
58	
59	void _leLabelWidget_GetTextRects(const leLabelWidget* lbl,
60	                                 leRect* boundingRect,
61	                                 leRect* kerningRect)
62	{
63	    leRect bounds;
64	    
65	    *boundingRect = leRect_Zero;
66	    
67	    if(lbl->string == NULL)
68	        return;
69	    
70	    lbl->string->fn->getRect(lbl->string,
71	                             boundingRect);
72	
73	    *kerningRect = *boundingRect;
74	
75	    leStringUtils_KerningRect((leRasterFont*)lbl->string->fn->getFont(lbl->string),
76	                              kerningRect);
77	    
78	    lbl->fn->localRect(lbl, &bounds);
79	    
80	    // arrange relative to image rect
81	    leUtils_ArrangeRectangleRelative(kerningRect,
82	                                     leRect_Zero,
83	                                     bounds,
84	                                     lbl->widget.style.halign,
85	                                     lbl->widget.style.valign,
86	                                     0,
87	                                     lbl->widget.margin.left,
88	                                     lbl->widget.margin.top,
89	                                     lbl->widget.margin.right,
90	                                     lbl->widget.margin.bottom,
91	                                     0);
92	
93	    boundingRect->x = kerningRect->x;
94	    boundingRect->y = kerningRect->y;
95	
96	    leRectClip(kerningRect, &bounds, kerningRect);
97		leRectClip(boundingRect, &bounds, boundingRect);
98	
99		// move the draw rect to screen space
100	    leUtils_RectToScreenSpace((leWidget*)lbl, kerningRect);
101	}
102	
103	static void drawBackground(leLabelWidget* lbl);
104	static void drawString(leLabelWidget* lbl);
105	static void drawBorder(leLabelWidget* lbl);
106	
107	
108	static void nextState(leLabelWidget* lbl)
109	{
110	    switch(lbl->widget.status.drawState)
111	    {
112	        case NOT_STARTED:
113	        {
114	            paintState.alpha = 255;
115	
116	#if LE_ALPHA_BLENDING_ENABLED == 1
117	            if(lbl->fn->getCumulativeAlphaEnabled(lbl) == LE_TRUE)
118	            {
119	                paintState.alpha = lbl->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount(lbl);
120	            }
121	#endif
122	            
123	            if(lbl->widget.style.backgroundType != LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE)
124	            {
125	                lbl->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BACKGROUND;
126	                lbl->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBackground;
127	
128	                return;
129	            }
130	        }
131	        // fall through
132	        case DRAW_BACKGROUND:
133	        {
134	            if(lbl->string != NULL && lbl->string->fn->isEmpty(lbl->string) == LE_FALSE)
135	            {
136	                lbl->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_STRING;
137	                lbl->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawString;
138	
139	                return;
140	            }
141	        }
142	        // fall through
143	        case DRAW_STRING:
144	        {
145	            if(lbl->widget.style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
146	            {
147	                lbl->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBorder;
148	                lbl->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BORDER;
149	                
150	                return;
151	            }
152	
153	
154	        }
155	        // fall through
156	        case DRAW_BORDER:
157	        {
158	            lbl->widget.status.drawState = DONE;
159	            lbl->widget.drawFunc = NULL;
160	        }
161	    }
162	}
163	
164	static void drawBackground(leLabelWidget* lbl)
165	{
166	    leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardBackground((leWidget*)lbl,
167	                                                paintState.alpha);
168	    
169	    nextState(lbl);
170	}
171	
172	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
173	static void onStringStreamFinished(leStreamManager* strm)
174	{
175	    leLabelWidget* lbl = (leLabelWidget*)strm->userData;
176	
177	    lbl->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_STRING;
178	
179	    nextState(lbl);
180	}
181	#endif
182	
183	static void drawString(leLabelWidget* lbl)
184	{
185	    leRect boundingRect = leRect_Zero;
186	    leRect kerningRect = leRect_Zero;
187	    leStringRenderRequest req;
188	
189	    _leLabelWidget_GetTextRects(lbl, &boundingRect, &kerningRect);
190	
191	    req.str = lbl->string;
192	    req.x = kerningRect.x;
193	    req.y = kerningRect.y;
194	    req.align = lbl->widget.style.halign;
195	    req.color = leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT);
196	    req.alpha = paintState.alpha;
197	    req.lookupTable = leUtils_GetSchemeLookupTable(lbl->widget.scheme,
198	                                                   req.color,
199	                                                   leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE));
200	
201	    leStringRenderer_DrawString(&req);
202	
203	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
204	    if(leGetActiveStream() != NULL)
205	    {
206	        leGetActiveStream()->onDone = onStringStreamFinished;
207	        leGetActiveStream()->userData = lbl;
208	
209	        lbl->widget.status.drawState = WAIT_STRING;
210	
211	        return;
212	    }
213	#endif
214	    
215	    nextState(lbl);
216	}
217	
218	static void drawBorder(leLabelWidget* lbl)
219	{
220	    if(lbl->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)
221	    {
222	        leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardLineBorder((leWidget*)lbl,
223	                                                    paintState.alpha);
224	    }
225	    else if(lbl->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL)
226	    {
227	        leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardRaisedBorder((leWidget*)lbl,
228	                                                      paintState.alpha);
229	    }
230	    
231	    nextState(lbl);
232	}
233	
234	void _leLabelWidget_Paint(leLabelWidget* lbl)
235	{
236	    if(lbl->widget.status.drawState == NOT_STARTED)
237	        nextState(lbl);
238	
239	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
240	    if(lbl->widget.status.drawState == WAIT_STRING)
241	        return;
242	#endif
243	
244	    while(lbl->widget.status.drawState != DONE)
245	    {
246	        lbl->widget.drawFunc((leWidget*)lbl);
247	        
248	#if LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL == 2
249	        break;
250	#endif
```

## Summary: Legato Screen Integration in Marvin Firmware

Based on my exploration of the marvin firmware, here's exactly how Legato screens are generated, wired, and how you can hook custom code:

### (a) Screen Generation Pattern

**File paths:**
- Generated screen header: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h`
- Generated screen implementation: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.c`
- Screen initialization/management: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.c`

**Generated Functions (from `le_gen_screen_Marvin.h`):**
```c
leResult screenInit_Marvin(void);         // called at Legato init
leResult screenShow_Marvin(void);         // called when screen becomes active
void screenHide_Marvin(void);             // called when screen is hidden
void screenDestroy_Marvin(void);          // called at Legato shutdown
void screenUpdate_Marvin(void);           // called every frame during Legato_Tasks()
leWidget* screenGetRoot_Marvin(uint32_t lyrIdx);  // gets root widget for layer
```

**Screen Structure:**
The Marvin screen has two layers (root0 for layer 0, root1 for layer 1):
- Each root is a static `leWidget*` created in `screenShow_Marvin()`
- Root0 contains the main dashboard (1280x800 at layer 0)
- Root1 contains the navigation panel (320x800 at layer 1)
- All widgets are declared as `extern leWidget*` in the header and allocated in `screenShow_Marvin()`
- Widgets are added via `parent->fn->addChild(parent, child)` call

**How widgets are added to parents (from line 304-308):**
```c
Marvin_PANEL_BASE = leWidget_New();
Marvin_PANEL_BASE->fn->setPosition(Marvin_PANEL_BASE, 0, 0);
Marvin_PANEL_BASE->fn->setSize(Marvin_PANEL_BASE, 1280, 800);
// ... configure widget ...
root0->fn->addChild(root0, (leWidget*)Marvin_PANEL_BASE);
```

**To add your custom widget as a child at runtime:**
```c
// Call from your code after screenShow_Marvin() runs:
leWidget* myCustomWidget = CustomScrollingList_New();
myCustomWidget->fn->setPosition(myCustomWidget, x, y);
myCustomWidget->fn->setSize(myCustomWidget, w, h);
Marvin_PANEL_BASE_CENTER->fn->addChild(Marvin_PANEL_BASE_CENTER, myCustomWidget);
```

**Screen-show hook mechanism:**
There is NO automatic screen-show hook in the generated code. However, you can:

1. **Modify the generated `le_gen_init.c`** (file: `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.c`, lines 64-76):

}

{
    switch(legatoState) {
        case LEGATO_STATE_INIT: { /* ... */ break; }
        case LEGATO_STATE_RUNNING:
        {
            legato_updateScreenState();  // Calls screenShow_Marvin() if screen changed
            leUpdate(0);                 // This is THE MAIN UPDATE CALL
            break;
        }
    }
}

```c

{

}
```

**`screenUpdate_Marvin()` called every frame (from `le_gen_init.c`, lines 82-95):**
```c

**For inertia animation, use the widget's `update()` vtable entry:**

When you create your custom scrolling widget, override its `update()` method:
```c
// In your custom widget implementation:
void CustomScrollList_Update(leWidget* _this, uint32_t dt)
{
    CustomScrollList* widget = (CustomScrollList*)_this;
    
    // dt is milliseconds since last call
    // Apply inertia decay:
    if(widget->velocityY != 0) {
        widget->offsetY += widget->velocityY * dt / 1000.0f;  // dt in ms
        widget->velocityY *= 0.95f;  // friction decay
        
        // Clamp to bounds
        if(widget->velocityY < 1 && widget->velocityY > -1) {
            widget->velocityY = 0;
        }
        
        widget->fn->invalidate(widget);  // Mark for redraw
    }
}
```

The `leUpdate()` call at the top level propagates down to every widget's `update()` method. From the widget vtable definition (`legato_widget.h`):
```c
void (*update)(THIS_TYPE* _this, uint32_t dt);  // Called every frame
```

**Summary of the timing:**
- `Legato_Tasks()` runs every 10 ms in FreeRTOS
- Each call to `Legato_Tasks()` calls `leUpdate(0)` 
- `leUpdate()` walks the widget tree and calls each widget's `update(dt)` method
- Your custom widget's `update()` is the hook for scroll inertia

### (d) Screen Switching Mechanism

**File:** `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.c`

**How screens are shown:**
```c
void legato_initializeScreenState(void)  // Called at startup
{
    screenInit_Screen0();
    screenInit_Marvin();
    legato_showScreen(screenID_Marvin);  // Show Marvin initially
}

void legato_showScreen(uint32_t id)
{
    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
        return;
    changingToScreen = id;  // Flag change (doesn't happen immediately)
}

void legato_updateScreenState(void)  // Called every frame
{
    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_TRUE)
        return;  // Can't change mid-render
    
    if(changingToScreen >= 0) {
        legato_hideCurrentScreen();
        leEvent_ClearList();
        
        switch(changingToScreen) {
            case screenID_Marvin:
                screenShow_Marvin();  // Creates all widgets
                break;
        }
        
        currentScreen = changingToScreen;
        changingToScreen = -1;
    }
    
    // Every frame, call the active screen's update
    switch(currentScreen) {
        case screenID_Marvin:
            screenUpdate_Marvin();  // 10ms tick
            break;
    }
}
```

**To get the active screen's root widget at runtime:**
```c
leWidget* root = screenGetRoot_Marvin(0);  // Layer 0
// or
leWidget* root = screenGetRoot_Marvin(1);  // Layer 1
```

There is **no explicit "touch capture" API** in this version. Touch is routed to the widget at the touch point. To implement drag/scroll:
- Track `touchID` across down → move → up events
- Use `prevX/prevY` vs current `x/y` to calculate deltas
- Store captured `touchID` in widget state to recognize subsequent moves from the same touch source

static void drawString(leLabelWidget* lbl)
{
    leRect boundingRect = leRect_Zero;
    leRect kerningRect = leRect_Zero;
    leStringRenderRequest req;

    // Get text layout
    _leLabelWidget_GetTextRects(lbl, &boundingRect, &kerningRect);

    // Fill render request
    req.str = lbl->string;
    req.x = kerningRect.x;
    req.y = kerningRect.y;
    req.align = lbl->widget.style.halign;
    req.color = leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT);
    req.alpha = paintState.alpha;  // cumulative alpha
    req.lookupTable = leUtils_GetSchemeLookupTable(
        lbl->widget.scheme,
        req.color,
        leScheme_GetRenderColor(lbl->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE));

    // Draw
    leStringRenderer_DrawString(&req);
}

void _leLabelWidget_Paint(leLabelWidget* lbl)
{
    // State machine: draw background → draw string → draw border
    while(lbl->widget.status.drawState != DONE) {
        lbl->widget.drawFunc((leWidget*)lbl);
    }
}

### Summary: Custom Scrollable List Widget Pattern

To build your custom scrollable list:

1. **Define struct** combining base + your fields:
   ```c
   typedef struct leScrollableListWidget {
       leWidget widget;
       const leScrollableListWidgetVTable* fn;
       // Your fields: item array, scroll offset, selection, etc.
   } leScrollableListWidget;
   ```

2. **Allocate & construct**:
   ```c
   leScrollableListWidget* list = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leScrollableListWidget));
   leWidget_Constructor((leWidget*)list);
   list->widget.fn = &vtable;
   list->fn = &vtable;
   list->widget.type = LE_WIDGET_CUSTOM;  // or custom enum
   ```

3. **Touch handling** (in `touchMoveEvent` vtable handler):
   - Track `touchID`, measure delta from `prevX/prevY` to `x/y`
   - Update `scroll_offset` based on delta
   - Call `list->fn->_damageArea(list, &list->widget.rect)` to trigger repaint

4. **Paint function** (vtable `_paint`):
   - Calculate visible item rects (clip to widget bounds)
   - For each visible item, call `leStringRenderer_DrawString()` with item text + font from scheme
   - Use `leScheme_GetRenderColor(widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_TEXT)` for text color

5. **Invalidate**:
   - When data changes: `widget.fn->invalidate(widget)`
   - Dirty rect for partial updates: `widget.fn->_damageArea(widget, &changedRect)`

All drawing clipping is automatic; child widgets' rects are clipped to parent bounds during render.

<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the widget get its row data?**

Options:
- **Row-provider callback** - Widget is generic: the screen registers a callback that fills a row-view {badge text+color, title, artist, right-text} for index i. Widget never includes catalog.h. Decouples it, lets the screen own catalog→row mapping (and future tier/setlist grouping), and is testable with a demo provider.
- **Bind directly to catalog** - Widget calls Catalog_Count()/Catalog_At() itself and formats rows internally. Less glue now, but couples the widget to the catalog and bakes row layout/duration formatting into it; harder to reuse or test in isolation.

**What scroll/touch behavior?**

Options:
- **Drag + inertia + tap-select** - Finger-follow drag; flick imparts momentum that decays (friction) and clamps at the ends; a touch that moves under a small threshold counts as a tap → selects the row + fires a selection-changed callback. Standard touchscreen feel; inertia runs in the update(dt) hook.
- **Drag + tap only** - Finger-follow drag with no momentum (stops when you lift), plus tap-to-select. Simpler — no velocity tracking or decay loop. Can add inertia later.

**How should the single widget instance be allocated? (static-allocation rule applies.)**

Options:
- **Legato pool (LE_MALLOC) once** - Allocate at create via Legato's widget pool, exactly like every MGS-generated widget — Legato manages its lifecycle (destroy frees it). One allocation, consistent with the existing Legato heap carve-out from the static rule. Not new malloc in a marvin subsystem.
- **Static construct-in-place** - File-scope static struct + run the constructor on it; strictly honors no-malloc. We own the single instance's lifetime and must keep it out of Legato's auto-destroy path (don't let a screen teardown free it).


**Answer:** Row-provider callback, Drag + inertia + tap-select, I'm tempted to say static. We'll only ever have one of these and the content won't really be changing past first load. But not sure if we should break from normal legato widget mechanism?
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-24 23:37:12Z)**_

That grep is decisive on the allocation question. Here's the verified teardown path:

- `screenHide_Marvin()` → `leWidget_Delete(root0)` → `_leWidget_Destructor` **recursively walks children, calling `child->fn->_destructor(child)` then `LE_FREE(child)`** ([legato_widget.c:150-152, 179-181](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.c)).

So any widget attached to a screen tree gets `LE_FREE`'d on screen hide. If that widget is statically allocated, you're handing a static pointer to the pool's free → heap corruption. Making static *safe* means detaching our widget before every screen hide — fighting the framework for no real gain.

So my recommendation flips your lean: **pool-allocate it, like every other Legato widget.** And crucially — this is *not* a deviation from the static-allocation rule. That rule governs marvin's own subsystems (tasks, queues, DMA buffers); the Legato widget tree is the already-accepted heap carve-out, and all ~50 MGS widgets on the screen are pool-allocated identically. We keep determinism by making the widget a **single self-contained allocation** — all scratch/row buffers are fixed-size arrays *inside* the widget struct, so it's one `LE_MALLOC` with no secondary allocations, created and freed as a unit with its screen. Net: no churn beyond what Legato already does for every widget, and no lifecycle hazard.

```md
# Song-select scrollable list — custom Legato widget (marvin operator UI)

## Context

The marvin operator UI needs a **SELECT SONG** screen (per Greg's mockup): a scrollable,
touch-driven setlist on the left, an album-art + metadata detail panel in the center, and
difficulty/mode/Select controls on the right. We're building the **scrolling list widget first** —
it's the primary, reusable piece; the surrounding screen is authored later in Microchip Graphics
Suite (MGS) by Greg.

Legato's stock `leListWidget` is disabled in `legato_config.h` and, even enabled, its item model is
icon + a single string — it can't render the rich row (color tier badge + bold title + dim artist +
right-aligned duration). So we build a **custom widget by subclassing `leWidget`**, living entirely
in our own `ui/song_list.{h,c}` — zero edits to the generated `gfx/legato/` tree (same MCC-isolation
discipline as `console`/`perf_log`; same reason we used embedded-cli over SYS_CONSOLE).

The detail panel (later) is the catalog's consumer (`Catalog_Lookup` → title/artist/album/year/genre/
bpm/length). The list rows reach the widget through a **provider callback**, so the widget never
includes `catalog.h` and is decoupled from both the catalog and the still-deferred tier/setlist model.

## Decisions (settled with Greg)

- **Custom `leWidget` subclass** (not the DrawSurface-callback route) — self-contained, no
  `legato_config.h` toggles, behaves like a built-in widget.
- **Row-provider callback** data model — widget is generic; the screen owns catalog→row mapping.
- **Drag + kinetic inertia + tap-to-select** touch behavior.
- **Pool-allocated (`LE_MALLOC`) like every Legato widget — NOT static.** Verified: `screenHide` →
  `leWidget_Delete(root)` → `_leWidget_Destructor` recursively `LE_FREE`s the whole child tree
  (`legato_widget.c:150-152,179-181`); a static widget attached to a screen would feed a static
  pointer to `LE_FREE` → pool corruption. This is not a deviation from the static-allocation rule
  (which governs marvin's own subsystems) — the Legato widget tree is the existing heap carve-out.
  Determinism is preserved by making the widget **one self-contained allocation**: all scratch/row
  buffers are fixed-size arrays inside the widget struct, no secondary mallocs, freed as a unit.

## The widget — `default/src/ui/song_list.{h,c}` (new; add to `user.cmake`)

Public API (no catalog dependency):

\```c
typedef struct {
    const char *badge;       /* e.g. "T1"; "" for none */
    leColor     badgeColor;  /* tier color */
    const char *title;
    const char *artist;
    const char *right;       /* right-aligned, e.g. "3:42" */
    bool        selected;
} songlist_row_t;

typedef bool (*songlist_row_fn)(void *ctx, int index, songlist_row_t *out); /* false if OOR */
typedef void (*songlist_select_fn)(void *ctx, int index);

leWidget *SongList_New(void);                                   /* pool-alloc + construct */
void SongList_SetModel(leWidget*, int count, songlist_row_fn, void *ctx);
void SongList_SetSelectHandler(leWidget*, songlist_select_fn, void *ctx);
void SongList_SetFonts(leWidget*, const leFont *title, const leFont *meta, const leFont *badge);
void SongList_SetRowHeight(leWidget*, int px);
int  SongList_Selected(const leWidget*);
void SongList_ScrollToSelected(leWidget*);
\```

`leSongListWidget` (subclasses `leWidget`, following the button-widget constructor/vtable pattern in
`widget/button/legato_widget_button.c`):
- base `leWidget widget;` + `const leSongListWidgetVTable *fn;`
- model: count, row fn + ctx, select fn + ctx
- view: `float scrollY`, `float velocity`, `rowHeight`, `selectedIndex`, font ptrs, colors
- touch: active touchID, `startY`/`lastY`, `dragging` flag, last-move dt for velocity
- one small fixed `char` scratch for any local formatting (provider supplies strings)

VTable overrides (reusing the renderer/string APIs confirmed present):
- `_paint`: `first = floor(scrollY/rowHeight)`; for each row intersecting the viewport — fill row bg
  (`leRenderer_RectFill`, highlight color if `selected`), draw badge (filled rect + centered
  `leStringRenderer_DrawCString`), title (left, title font), artist (left, meta font, dim), `right`
  (right-aligned, meta font). Child clipping to the widget rect is automatic. Optional thin
  right-edge scroll indicator.
- `touchDownEvent`: capture `touchID`, record `startY`/`lastY`, zero `velocity`, clear `dragging`.
- `touchMoveEvent`: `scrollY -= (y-lastY)`; clamp `[0, maxScroll]`; update `velocity` from `dy/dt`;
  set `dragging` once movement exceeds a small tap threshold; `invalidate`.
- `touchUpEvent`: if not `dragging` → tap: hit-test `y`→index, set `selectedIndex`, fire select
  callback, `invalidate`; else keep `velocity` for inertia.
- `update(dt)`: if `velocity != 0` → `scrollY -= velocity*dt`; friction decay; clamp at ends (zero
  velocity on hit); `invalidate`; stop under an epsilon. (`update(dt)` is called every Legato tick,
  ~10 ms, via `leUpdate` — confirmed.)

`maxScroll = max(0, count*rowHeight - viewportH)`. Reuses: `leWidget_Constructor` + vtable copy,
`leStringRenderer_DrawCString`, `leRenderer_RectFill`, `leScheme_GetRenderColor`, `invalidate`. Fonts
come from `le_gen_assets.h` (`NotoSans_Regular_12..28`, `figmaFont_Menlo_*`), passed in via
`SongList_SetFonts` — Greg can add fonts as needed.

## Bring-up / verification (widget-first; song-select screen not built yet)

- **Temporary demo attach** — `default/src/ui/song_list_demo.c` (clearly marked scaffolding): builds
  the widget, installs a **catalog-backed provider** (`count = Catalog_Count()`; row `i` ←
  `Catalog_At(i)`: title/artist, `right` = `mm:ss` from `length_s`, `badge=""` for now since tier is
  deferred), attaches it to a visible root (`screenGetRoot_Marvin(0)` once the root exists, or an
  MGS host panel), and logs the chosen song from the select callback. Removed when the real
  song-select screen lands.
- On hardware: drag scrolls, flick imparts inertia that decays + clamps, tap selects (row highlights)
  and logs the song; exercise against the full 64-song catalog. Standard MPLAB-build + on-hardware
  loop; syntax-checked here against stubbed Legato headers where possible.

## Out of scope (later, separate work)

- The song-select **screen layout** in MGS (album art, catalog-fed metadata panel, difficulty/mode
  buttons, Select) — Greg authors it; binds the detail panel via `Catalog_Lookup` and the widget's
  select callback. The widget is built to drop into that screen.
- **Tier / career-setlist data model** + the deferred `tier` catalog column — badges render blank
  until then (the provider supplies badge text/color, so the widget needs no change when tier lands).
- Scrollbar styling polish, over-scroll rubber-band, snap-to-row.

Plan is written. Quick summary of what it lands:

- **`ui/song_list.{h,c}`** — a custom `leSongListWidget` (subclasses `leWidget`, button-widget pattern), entirely in our tree, no generated-file edits.
- **Decoupled via a row-provider callback** — widget never touches `catalog.h`; the screen maps catalog→rows (and supplies tier badges later).
- **Touch:** drag + kinetic inertia (in the per-frame `update(dt)` hook) + tap-to-select with a selection callback.
- **Paint:** `leRenderer_RectFill` for row highlight + badge, `leStringRenderer_DrawCString` for title/artist/duration using existing fonts — virtualized to visible rows, auto-clipped.
- **Pool-allocated** as a single self-contained allocation (fixed internal arrays), per the verified teardown finding — keeps determinism without fighting Legato's `LE_FREE`-on-hide.
- **Bring-up:** a temporary catalog-backed demo attach so we can validate scroll/inertia/tap on hardware against the 64-song catalog before the real MGS screen exists.
- **Out of scope:** the MGS screen layout, the tier/setlist data model (badges blank until then), and scroll polish.

```text
static struct
{
    uint32_t alpha;
} paintState;

static void drawBackground(leWidget* wdg);
static void drawBorder(leWidget* wdg);

static void drawBackground(leWidget* wdg)
{
    //printf("button painting\n");
    
    if(wdg->style.backgroundType == LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_FILL)
    {
        //Only support round corners for no or line borders
        if (wdg->style.cornerRadius > 0 &&
            (wdg->style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE ||
             wdg->style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE))
        {
            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawRoundCornerBackground(wdg,
                                                           leScheme_GetRenderColor(wdg->scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE),
                                                           paintState.alpha);
        }
        else
        {
            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground(wdg,
                                                leScheme_GetRenderColor(wdg->scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE),
                                                paintState.alpha);
        }
    }

    if(wdg->style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
    {
        wdg->status.drawState = DRAW_BORDER;
        wdg->drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBorder;
    }
    else
    {
        wdg->status.drawState = DONE;
        wdg->drawFunc = NULL;
        
        return;
    }
    
#if LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL < 2
    wdg->drawFunc((leWidget*)wdg);
#endif
}

static void drawBorder(leWidget* wdg)
{
    if(wdg->style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)
    {
        leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardLineBorder(wdg, paintState.alpha);
    }
    else if(wdg->style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL)
    {
        leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawStandardRaisedBorder(wdg, paintState.alpha);
    }
        
    wdg->status.drawState = DONE;
    wdg->drawFunc = NULL;
}

void _leWidget_Paint(leWidget* wdg)
{
    switch(wdg->status.drawState)
    {
        case NOT_STARTED:
        {
            paintState.alpha = 255;

#if LE_ALPHA_BLENDING_ENABLED == 1
            if(wdg->fn->getCumulativeAlphaEnabled(wdg) == LE_TRUE)
            {
                paintState.alpha = wdg->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount(wdg);
            }
#endif

            wdg->drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr) &drawBackground;

            break;
        }
        case DONE:
        {
            return;
        }
        default:
        { }
    }

    wdg->drawFunc((leWidget*)wdg);
}
```

void _leButtonWidget_GenerateVTable(void)
{
    _leWidget_FillVTable((void*)&buttonWidgetVTable);
    
    /* overrides from base class */
    buttonWidgetVTable._destructor = _leButtonWidget_Destructor;
    buttonWidgetVTable.languageChangeEvent = languageChanging;
    buttonWidgetVTable._paint = _leButtonWidget_Paint;
    buttonWidgetVTable.invalidateContents = invalidateContents;
    buttonWidgetVTable._invalidateBorderAreas = _leButtonWidget_InvalidateBorderAreas;
    buttonWidgetVTable.touchDownEvent = touchDown;
    buttonWidgetVTable.touchUpEvent = touchUp;
    buttonWidgetVTable.touchMoveEvent = touchMoved;
    
    /* member functions */
    buttonWidgetVTable.getToggleable = getToggleable;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setToggleable = setToggleable;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getPressed = getPressed;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setPressed = setPressed;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getString = getString;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setString = setString;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getPressedImage = getPressedImage;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setPressedImage = setPressedImage;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getReleasedImage = getReleasedImage;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setReleasedImage = setReleasedImage;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getImagePosition = getImagePosition;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setImagePosition = setImagePosition;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getImageMargin = getImageMargin;
    buttonWidgetVTable.setImageMargin = setImageMargin;
    buttonWidgetVTable.getPressedOffset = getPressedOffset;

    buttonWidgetVTable.setPressedEventCallback = setPressedEventCallback;

#ifndef MARVIN_UI_SONG_LIST_H
#define MARVIN_UI_SONG_LIST_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"   /* leWidget, leColor, leFont */

/* Scrollable, touch-driven song list (a custom leWidget subclass) for the
 * SELECT SONG screen — spec §4.8, mockup. Decoupled from the catalog: the owner
 * registers a row-provider that fills each visible row on demand, so the widget
 * never depends on game/catalog.h and the screen owns the catalog -> row mapping
 * (and the eventual tier/setlist grouping).
 *
 * Interaction: drag scrolls (content follows the finger) with kinetic inertia on
 * release; a touch that barely moves is a tap and selects that row, firing the
 * select handler. Painted virtualized — only visible rows are drawn, via the
 * Legato renderer (no per-row child widgets).
 *
 * Allocated from the Legato widget pool like every MGS widget (one
 * self-contained allocation; all state lives in the widget struct). Attach with
 * the usual parent->fn->addChild(parent, SongList_New()); Legato owns its
 * lifetime and frees it on screen teardown. */

typedef struct
{
    const char *badge;       /* short tier tag drawn in badgeColor, e.g. "T1"; "" / NULL = none */
    leColor     badgeColor;  /* RGB_888 (0xRRGGBB) text color for the badge */
    const char *title;
    const char *artist;
    const char *right;       /* right-aligned cell, e.g. "3:42"; NULL / "" = none */
    bool        selected;    /* set by the widget before paint; providers may ignore it */
} songlist_row_t;

/* Fill *out for row `index`; return false if index is out of range. Called
 * during paint for visible rows only — keep it cheap and non-blocking. */
typedef bool (*songlist_row_fn)(void *ctx, int index, songlist_row_t *out);

/* Fired when a tap changes the selection. */
typedef void (*songlist_select_fn)(void *ctx, int index);

leWidget *SongList_New(void);

void SongList_SetModel(leWidget *w, int count, songlist_row_fn rows, void *ctx);
void SongList_SetSelectHandler(leWidget *w, songlist_select_fn fn, void *ctx);
void SongList_SetFonts(leWidget *w, const leFont *title, const leFont *meta, const leFont *badge);
void SongList_SetRowHeight(leWidget *w, int px);

int  SongList_Selected(const leWidget *w);
void SongList_SetSelected(leWidget *w, int index);   /* programmatic; scrolls into view */

#endif

```c
#include "ui/song_list.h"

#include <string.h>

#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"
#include "gfx/legato/string/legato_string_renderer.h"

/* Internal helper defined in legato_widget.c (forward-declared per widget, the
 * same way the built-in widgets reach it). Copies the base widget vtable so we
 * can override only the slots we care about. */
void _leWidget_FillVTable(leWidgetVTable* tbl);

/* ---- layout / feel constants ------------------------------------------- */

#define SL_PAD_X        20      /* left/right inset for content */
#define SL_BADGE_COL    50      /* width reserved for the tier badge column */
#define SL_LINE_GAP     2       /* px between title and artist */
#define SL_TAP_SLOP     10      /* drag under this many px counts as a tap */
#define SL_FRICTION     0.88f   /* per-tick momentum decay */
#define SL_MIN_VEL      0.5f    /* momentum below this stops */
#define SL_DEFAULT_ROWH 64

/* Colors are authored in RGB_888 and converted to the active layer mode at
 * paint time. */
#define SL_BG           0x0E0E0Eu
#define SL_SEP          0x232323u
#define SL_SEL_BG       0xF2F2F2u
#define SL_TITLE        0xF0F0F0u
#define SL_ARTIST       0x8A8A8Au
#define SL_RIGHT        0x9A9A9Au
#define SL_SEL_TITLE    0x121212u
#define SL_SEL_ARTIST   0x606060u
#define SL_SEL_RIGHT    0x404040u

/* ---- widget type -------------------------------------------------------- */

typedef struct leSongListWidget
{
    leWidget widget;            /* base — must be first */

    int                count;
    songlist_row_fn    rowFn;
    void              *rowCtx;
    songlist_select_fn selFn;
    void              *selCtx;

    const leFont *titleFont;
    const leFont *metaFont;
    const leFont *badgeFont;

    int   rowHeight;
    float scrollY;              /* px scrolled from the top */
    float momentum;             /* px/tick, applied while not touching */
    int   selected;             /* -1 = none */

    /* touch tracking */
    bool    tracking;
    int32_t touchId;
    int32_t firstY;
    int32_t lastY;
} leSongListWidget;

static leWidgetVTable songListVTable;
static bool           vtableReady = false;

/* ---- small helpers ------------------------------------------------------ */

static leColor conv(leColor rgb888)
{
    return leColorConvert(LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888, leRenderer_CurrentColorMode(), rgb888);
}

static int font_h(const leFont *f)
{
    return (f != NULL) ? (int)((const leRasterFont *)f)->height : 0;
}

static int max_scroll(const leSongListWidget *w)
{
    int content = w->count * w->rowHeight;
    int vh = (int)w->widget.rect.height;
    return (content > vh) ? (content - vh) : 0;
}

static void clamp_scroll(leSongListWidget *w)
{
    int mx = max_scroll(w);
    if (w->scrollY < 0.0f)        { w->scrollY = 0.0f; }
    else if (w->scrollY > (float)mx) { w->scrollY = (float)mx; }
}

static void draw_str(const leSongListWidget *w, const char *s, const leFont *font,
                     int x, int y, leHAlignment align, leColor color)
{
    leCStringRenderRequest req;
    if (s == NULL || s[0] == '\0' || font == NULL) { return; }

    req.str   = s;
    req.font  = font;
    req.x     = x;
    req.y     = y;
    req.align = align;
    req.color = color;
    req.alpha = 255;
    req.lookupTable = (w->widget.scheme != NULL)
        ? leUtils_GetSchemeLookupTable(w->widget.scheme, color,
              leScheme_GetRenderColor(w->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE))
        : NULL;

    leStringRenderer_DrawCString(&req);
}

/* ---- paint -------------------------------------------------------------- */

static void sl_paint(leWidget *wgt)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    leRect area;
    int rowH, vh, sy, first, firstTop, i;
    int titleH, metaH;

    if (wgt->status.drawState == LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE) { return; }

    wgt->fn->rectToScreen(wgt, &area);

    leRenderer_RectFill(&area, conv(SL_BG), 255);

    rowH = w->rowHeight;
    vh   = (int)area.height;
    if (rowH <= 0)
    {
        wgt->status.drawState = LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE;
        wgt->drawFunc = NULL;
        return;
    }

    titleH = font_h(w->titleFont);
    metaH  = font_h(w->metaFont);

    sy       = (int)(w->scrollY + 0.5f);
    first    = sy / rowH;
    if (first < 0) { first = 0; }
    firstTop = area.y - (sy - first * rowH);

    for (i = first; i < w->count; i++)
    {
        int rowTop = firstTop + (i - first) * rowH;
        songlist_row_t row;
        leColor titleC, artistC, rightC;
        int textX, block, startY;

        if (rowTop >= area.y + vh) { break; }

        memset(&row, 0, sizeof(row));
        if (w->rowFn == NULL || !w->rowFn(w->rowCtx, i, &row)) { continue; }
        row.selected = (i == w->selected);

        if (row.selected)
        {
            leRect hl = { area.x + 6, rowTop + 4, area.width - 12, rowH - 8 };
            leRenderer_RectFill(&hl, conv(SL_SEL_BG), 255);
            titleC = conv(SL_SEL_TITLE); artistC = conv(SL_SEL_ARTIST); rightC = conv(SL_SEL_RIGHT);
        }
        else
        {
            titleC = conv(SL_TITLE); artistC = conv(SL_ARTIST); rightC = conv(SL_RIGHT);

            leRect sep = { area.x + SL_PAD_X, rowTop + rowH - 1,
                           area.width - 2 * SL_PAD_X, 1 };
            leRenderer_RectFill(&sep, conv(SL_SEP), 255);
        }

        if (row.badge != NULL && row.badge[0] != '\0')
        {
            draw_str(w, row.badge, w->badgeFont,
                     area.x + SL_PAD_X, rowTop + (rowH - font_h(w->badgeFont)) / 2,
                     LE_HALIGN_LEFT, conv(row.badgeColor));
        }

        textX  = area.x + SL_PAD_X + SL_BADGE_COL;
        block  = titleH + SL_LINE_GAP + metaH;
        startY = rowTop + (rowH - block) / 2;

        draw_str(w, row.title,  w->titleFont, textX, startY, LE_HALIGN_LEFT, titleC);
        draw_str(w, row.artist, w->metaFont,  textX, startY + titleH + SL_LINE_GAP,
                 LE_HALIGN_LEFT, artistC);
        draw_str(w, row.right,  w->metaFont,
                 area.x + area.width - SL_PAD_X, rowTop + (rowH - metaH) / 2,
                 LE_HALIGN_RIGHT, rightC);
    }

    wgt->status.drawState = LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE;
    wgt->drawFunc = NULL;
}

/* ---- touch + inertia ---------------------------------------------------- */

static void sl_touchDown(leWidget *wgt, leWidgetEvent_TouchDown *evt)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;

    w->tracking = true;
    w->touchId  = evt->touchID;
    w->firstY   = evt->y;
    w->lastY    = evt->y;
    w->momentum = 0.0f;

    leWidgetEvent_Accept((leWidgetEvent *)evt, wgt);
}

static void sl_touchMove(leWidget *wgt, leWidgetEvent_TouchMove *evt)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    int dy;

    if (!w->tracking || (int32_t)evt->touchID != w->touchId) { return; }

    dy = evt->y - w->lastY;            /* finger down (dy>0) reveals earlier rows */
    w->scrollY -= (float)dy;
    w->momentum = (float)dy;           /* carried into inertia on release */
    w->lastY    = evt->y;

    clamp_scroll(w);
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
    leWidgetEvent_Accept((leWidgetEvent *)evt, wgt);
}

static void sl_touchUp(leWidget *wgt, leWidgetEvent_TouchUp *evt)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;

    if (w->tracking && (int32_t)evt->touchID == w->touchId)
    {
        int moved = evt->y - w->firstY;
        if (moved < 0) { moved = -moved; }

        if (moved < SL_TAP_SLOP)
        {
            /* tap: select the row under the touch */
            leRect area;
            int contentY, idx;

            wgt->fn->rectToScreen(wgt, &area);
            contentY = (evt->y - area.y) + (int)(w->scrollY + 0.5f);
            idx = (w->rowHeight > 0) ? contentY / w->rowHeight : -1;

            if (idx >= 0 && idx < w->count && idx != w->selected)
            {
                w->selected = idx;
                if (w->selFn != NULL) { w->selFn(w->selCtx, idx); }
                wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
            }
            w->momentum = 0.0f;        /* no fling on a tap */
        }
        /* else: leave momentum for the inertia loop */

        w->tracking = false;
    }

    leWidgetEvent_Accept((leWidgetEvent *)evt, wgt);
}

static void sl_update(leWidget *wgt, uint32_t dt)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    (void)dt;   /* fixed ~10 ms Legato tick; momentum is in px/tick */

    if (w->tracking || w->momentum == 0.0f) { return; }

    w->scrollY -= w->momentum;
    w->momentum *= SL_FRICTION;
    if (w->momentum < SL_MIN_VEL && w->momentum > -SL_MIN_VEL) { w->momentum = 0.0f; }

    {
        int mx = max_scroll(w);
        if (w->scrollY < 0.0f || w->scrollY > (float)mx) { w->momentum = 0.0f; }
    }
    clamp_scroll(w);
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
}

/* ---- construction ------------------------------------------------------- */

static void gen_vtable(void)
{
    if (vtableReady) { return; }
    _leWidget_FillVTable(&songListVTable);
    songListVTable._paint         = sl_paint;
    songListVTable.update         = sl_update;
    songListVTable.touchDownEvent = sl_touchDown;
    songListVTable.touchMoveEvent = sl_touchMove;
    songListVTable.touchUpEvent   = sl_touchUp;
    vtableReady = true;
}

leWidget *SongList_New(void)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leSongListWidget));
    if (w == NULL) { return NULL; }

    gen_vtable();

    leWidget_Constructor(&w->widget);
    w->widget.fn = &songListVTable;
    w->widget.type = LE_WIDGET_PANEL;
    w->widget.style.backgroundType = LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE;  /* we paint our own */
    if (w->widget.scheme == NULL) { w->widget.scheme = leGetDefaultScheme(); }

    w->count     = 0;
    w->rowFn     = NULL;  w->rowCtx = NULL;
    w->selFn     = NULL;  w->selCtx = NULL;
    w->titleFont = NULL;  w->metaFont = NULL;  w->badgeFont = NULL;
    w->rowHeight = SL_DEFAULT_ROWH;
    w->scrollY   = 0.0f;
    w->momentum  = 0.0f;
    w->selected  = -1;
    w->tracking  = false;
    w->touchId   = 0;
    w->firstY    = 0;
    w->lastY     = 0;

    return &w->widget;
}

/* ---- public setters/getters -------------------------------------------- */

void SongList_SetModel(leWidget *wgt, int count, songlist_row_fn rows, void *ctx)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    if (w == NULL) { return; }
    w->count  = (count > 0) ? count : 0;
    w->rowFn  = rows;
    w->rowCtx = ctx;
    w->scrollY = 0.0f;
    w->momentum = 0.0f;
    clamp_scroll(w);
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
}

void SongList_SetSelectHandler(leWidget *wgt, songlist_select_fn fn, void *ctx)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    if (w == NULL) { return; }
    w->selFn  = fn;
    w->selCtx = ctx;
}

void SongList_SetFonts(leWidget *wgt, const leFont *title, const leFont *meta, const leFont *badge)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    if (w == NULL) { return; }
    w->titleFont = title;
    w->metaFont  = meta;
    w->badgeFont = badge;
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
}

void SongList_SetRowHeight(leWidget *wgt, int px)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    if (w == NULL || px <= 0) { return; }
    w->rowHeight = px;
    clamp_scroll(w);
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
}

int SongList_Selected(const leWidget *wgt)
{
    const leSongListWidget *w = (const leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    return (w != NULL) ? w->selected : -1;
}

void SongList_SetSelected(leWidget *wgt, int index)
{
    leSongListWidget *w = (leSongListWidget *)wgt;
    if (w == NULL || index < 0 || index >= w->count) { return; }

    w->selected = index;

    /* scroll the selected row fully into view */
    {
        int rowTop = index * w->rowHeight;
        int rowBot = rowTop + w->rowHeight;
        int vh     = (int)w->widget.rect.height;
        if (rowTop < (int)w->scrollY)            { w->scrollY = (float)rowTop; }
        else if (rowBot > (int)w->scrollY + vh)  { w->scrollY = (float)(rowBot - vh); }
        clamp_scroll(w);
    }
    wgt->fn->invalidate(wgt);
}

```c
#include "ui/song_list_demo.h"

#include <stdio.h>

#include "ui/song_list.h"
#include "game/catalog.h"
#include "log.h"

#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_assets.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h"

static leWidget *s_list = NULL;

static bool demo_row(void *ctx, int index, songlist_row_t *out)
{
    (void)ctx;
    const catalog_entry_t *e = Catalog_At(index);
    static char dur[8];

    if (e == NULL) { return false; }

    if (e->length_s != 0)
    {
        (void)snprintf(dur, sizeof(dur), "%u:%02u",
                       (unsigned)(e->length_s / 60u), (unsigned)(e->length_s % 60u));
    }
    else { dur[0] = '\0'; }

    out->title      = e->title;
    out->artist     = e->artist;
    out->right      = dur;
    out->badge      = "";        /* tier deferred — no badge yet */
    out->badgeColor = 0;
    return true;
}

static void demo_select(void *ctx, int index)
{
    (void)ctx;
    const catalog_entry_t *e = Catalog_At(index);
    LOG_INFO("songlist: selected #%d  %s - %s\r\n", index,
             (e != NULL) ? e->title : "?", (e != NULL) ? e->artist : "?");
}

void SongList_DemoAttach(void)
{
    leWidget *root;
    int n;

    if (s_list != NULL) { LOG_INFO("songlist: already attached\r\n"); return; }

    (void)Catalog_Reload();
    n = Catalog_Count();

    root = screenGetRoot_Marvin(0);
    if (root == NULL) { LOG_WARN("songlist: Marvin screen not shown\r\n"); return; }

    s_list = SongList_New();
    if (s_list == NULL) { LOG_WARN("songlist: widget alloc failed\r\n"); return; }

    s_list->fn->setPosition(s_list, 40, 80);
    s_list->fn->setSize(s_list, 560, 640);
    SongList_SetFonts(s_list,
                      (const leFont *)&NotoSans_Regular_20,
                      (const leFont *)&NotoSans_Regular_14,
                      (const leFont *)&figmaFont_Menlo_14);
    SongList_SetRowHeight(s_list, 64);
    SongList_SetModel(s_list, n, demo_row, NULL);
    SongList_SetSelectHandler(s_list, demo_select, NULL);

    root->fn->addChild(root, s_list);
    LOG_INFO("songlist: attached, %d song(s)\r\n", n);
}

Fixed. Reworked the vtable setup in [song_list.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/song_list.c):

- Dropped the `_leWidget_FillVTable` forward-declaration and `gen_vtable()` — that function only exists when `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES == 1`, and this project builds with it `== 0` (static const vtables), so the symbol wasn't linkable.

This is actually more robust than the original: it grabs whatever the real base vtable is at runtime — no enumerating ~70 base slots, and it works under either `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES` setting. Re-checked clean against the stub.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 00:04:08Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 00:04:18Z)**_

Yes — for this case the local copy is the better call. The two approaches differ a lot in blast radius:

**Enabling `LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES`** is a *global* Legato switch. It changes how **every** widget builds its vtable — button, label, image, all of them flip from static-const to runtime-filled. Consequences:
- **RAM cost across the board.** Static const vtables live in flash (`.rodata`), shared, zero RAM. Dynamic mode fills each widget type's vtable (~70 pointers) into RAM at init. So you'd move *all* stock widget vtables flash→RAM to serve one custom widget.
- **MGS-coupled + regen risk.** `legato_config.h` is generated, so the flag should be flipped in MGS (not hand-edited, or it's a re-apply patch against the no-patch discipline), and the generated init has to call every `*_GenerateVTable()`. Bigger surface for a regen to disturb.
- It's a project-wide behavioral change to fix a one-widget problem.

**The runtime copy** is local and cheap:
- One mutable vtable in RAM (~280 B) for just our widget; everything else stays static-const in flash.
- **Mode-agnostic** — if you ever do flip the global flag in MGS, our code still works unchanged (it just copies whatever base vtable exists).
- **Regen-robust** — it copies the *live* base vtable, so if a Legato update adds a vtable slot, we automatically inherit the base's function for it.

There's a third option I didn't take: a **full static-const vtable initializer** for our widget (enumerate all ~70 base slots + our overrides, like the button does). That's the "purest" static-mode idiom and keeps the vtable in flash (saves the ~280 B RAM). But it's verbose and *more* fragile to regen — if Legato adds/reorders a slot, an un-listed slot is left `NULL` and the framework could call through it → crash. The copy approach can't have that hole.

So the ranking for one custom widget: **runtime copy (robust, local, ~280 B RAM) > full static initializer (flash, verbose, regen-fragile) > enabling dynamic globally (project-wide RAM + coupling).** If RAM ever got tight and you wanted that 280 B back, switching our widget to the full static initializer is the move — not flipping the global flag.

Let me get the real numbers first. Found it:

- `Legato_Tasks()` calls **`leUpdate(0)`** — the `dt` handed to every `update()` is literally **0** ([le_gen_harmony.c:83](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_harmony.c)). So my `(void)dt` was right, but it means I was advancing momentum a fixed amount **per loop iteration**, not per unit time.
- The loop is `Legato_Tasks(); vTaskDelay(10ms)` — so ~10 ms *sleep* plus the render pass, and rendering is capped at the 55 Hz panel. Net: the real cadence is render-bound (~55 Hz) **and irregular** (the Legato task sits at priority 2, so vision/wire tasks preempt it).

That irregular, assumed-fixed cadence is exactly your "jumpy/slow." The fix is to stop assuming a tick and **measure real elapsed time** (FreeRTOS tick), making motion frame-rate-independent. Let me rework the scroll/inertia to be time-based.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 00:20:54Z)**_

Both questions answered, both with fixes applied:

## 1. Update rate → scrolling fix
**What I had assumed:** a fixed ~10 ms tick. **Reality:** `Legato_Tasks()` calls `leUpdate(0)`, so the `dt` handed to `update()` is always **0**, and the loop is `vTaskDelay(10ms)` + a render pass that's capped at the 55 Hz panel and **irregular** (Legato is priority-2, preempted by vision/wire). I was advancing momentum a fixed step *per loop iteration*, so when the iteration rate wobbled, so did the scroll → jumpy/slow.

**Fix (in [song_list.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/song_list.c)):** made motion **time-based** off the real FreeRTOS tick (`xTaskGetTickCount`):
- Drag stays 1:1 with the finger; release velocity is now captured in **px/ms** (`dy/dt`).
- Inertia integrates `scrollY += velocity·dt_ms` with time-based decay, so it's identical whether frames land at 30 or 60 Hz.
- Tunables up top: `SL_DECAY_PER_MS` (0.004 ≈ ½–¾ s glide), `SL_MAX_VEL` (4 px/ms fling cap), `SL_MAX_DT_MS` (100, guards a scheduling stall from leaping).

One caveat: *drag* smoothness is still bounded by repaint throughput (≈10 rows × 4 strings re-rendered per frame). If it still feels steppy while dragging, that's render cost, not the math — and it'll ease on a dedicated screen. Easy levers if needed: fewer visible rows, lighter rows.

## 2. Show-through → also fixed
Confirmed in `_leWidget_IsOpaque()`: a widget with `backgroundType == NONE` is treated as **transparent**, so Legato doesn't guarantee covering it when the dashboard behind repaints. I'd set `NONE` ("we paint our own"), but since `sl_paint` fills the whole rect opaquely every frame, the accurate flag is `FILL`. I switched it — and because we fully override `_paint`, that only flips the opacity bookkeeping (Legato now repaints us over anything behind); it adds **no** base background draw. So it's correct on the dedicated screen *and* clean if it ever overlays something.

Both re-checked clean against the stub. Give it another run — curious whether the time-based inertia feels right and whether drag is now smooth or still repaint-bound.

=== leRenderer_DamageArea ===
leResult leRenderer_DamageArea(const leRect* rect,
                               uint32_t layerIdx)
{
    leRect clipRect;
    leLayerState* layerState;
    leRenderLayerState* renderLayerState;

    if(layerIdx >= _state->layerList.size)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    layerState = leGetLayerState(layerIdx);
    
    // make sure rect is inside the layer
    if(leRectIntersects(&layerState->root.rect, rect) == LE_FALSE)
        return LE_FAILURE;
    
    // clip the incoming rectangle
    leRectClip(&layerState->root.rect, rect, &clipRect);

    renderLayerState = (leRenderLayerState*)layerState->rendererData;

    // initiate a new render frame if necessary
    if(_rendererState.frameState <= LE_FRAME_PREFRAME)
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_PREFRAME;

        // drawing not in progress, add the rectangle to the current list
        addDamageRectToList(&renderLayerState->currentDamageRects, &clipRect);
    }
    else
    {
        //printf("added pending rect\n");
        
        // there is a frame in progress, add to the list that will be processed
        // next time around
        addDamageRectToList(&renderLayerState->pendingDamageRects, &clipRect);
    }
    
    return LE_SUCCESS;
}

static leResult preFrame(void)
{
    _rendererState.layerIdx = 0;

    /*if(_rendererState.renderBuffer != NULL)
    {
        _rendererState.renderBuffer->mode = -1;
    }*/

    _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_PRELAYER;
    
    return LE_SUCCESS;
}

static void preLayer(void)
{
    uint32_t i;
    leRect rect;

#if LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_PADDING == 1
    uint32_t padSize = 0;
#endif

    //printf("dump: %i\n", dump++);

    _rendererState.currentLayerState = leGetLayerState(_rendererState.layerIdx);
    _rendererState.currentRenderLayer = (leRenderLayerState*)_rendererState.currentLayerState->rendererData;

    leRectArray_Clear(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList);
    leRectArray_Clear(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList);

    maxScratchPixels = (SCRATCH_BUFFER_SZ * 8) / leColorInfoTable[leGetLayerColorMode(_rendererState.layerIdx)].bpp;

    // merge rectangle lists
    if(_rendererState.bufferCount > 1)
    {
        for(i = 0; i < _rendererState.currentRenderLayer->prevDamageRects.size; i++)
        {
            leRectArray_PushBack(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList,
                                 &_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->prevDamageRects.rects[i]);
        }
    }

    for(i = 0; i < _rendererState.currentRenderLayer->currentDamageRects.size; i++)
    {
        leRectArray_PushBack(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList,
                             &_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->currentDamageRects.rects[i]);
    }

    if(_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList.size == 0)
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTLAYER;

        return;
    }

    // remove duplicate rectangles from combined list
    leRectArray_RemoveDuplicates(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList);

    // combine any adjacent rectangles
    leRectArray_MergeSimilar(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList);

    // remove overlapping space
    leRectArray_RemoveOverlapping(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList);

    // crop to scratch buffer size limit
    if(leGetLayerRenderHorizontal(_rendererState.layerIdx) == LE_TRUE)
    {
        // sort frame rects by X
        leRectArray_CropToSizeX(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList, maxScratchPixels);
    }
    else
    {
        // sort frame rects by Y
        leRectArray_CropToSizeY(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList, maxScratchPixels);
    }
    
#if LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_PADDING == 1
    if(leGetLayerColorMode(_rendererState.layerIdx) == LE_COLOR_MODE_MONOCHROME)
    {
        leRectArray_PadXToSize(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList, 8);
    }
    else
    {
        padSize = (leGetLayerColorMode(_rendererState.layerIdx) == LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565) ? 8 : 4;

#if LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 90 || LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 270
        leRectArray_PadRectangleHeight(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList,
                                       padSize);
#else
        leRectArray_PadRectangleWidth(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList,
                                      padSize);
#endif
    }
#endif

    while(_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList.size != 0)
    {
        rect = _rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList.rects[0];

        leRectArray_RemoveAt(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList, 0);

        addRectToFrameList(&rect);
    }

    if(leGetLayerRenderHorizontal(_rendererState.layerIdx) == LE_TRUE)
    {
        // sort frame rects by X
        leRectArray_SortByX(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList);
    }
    else
    {
        // sort frame rects by Y
        leRectArray_SortByY(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList);
    }

    _rendererState.frameRectIdx = 0;
    _rendererState.frameDrawCount = 0;

    if(_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList.size == 0)
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTLAYER;
    }
    else
    {
        _leRenderer_InitDrawForMode(leGetLayerColorMode(_rendererState.layerIdx));

        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_PRERECT;
    }
}

static void invalidateWidget(leWidget* wgt, leRect* rect)
{
    uint32_t idx;
    leRect localRect;
    leRect clipRect;
    
    if(LE_TEST_FLAG(wgt->flags, LE_WIDGET_VISIBLE) == LE_FALSE)
    {
        wgt->fn->_validateChildren(wgt);

        return;
    }

    localRect = wgt->rect;

    if(leRectIntersects(&localRect, rect) == LE_TRUE)
    {
        wgt->fn->_setDirtyState(wgt, LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_DIRTY);
        
        for(idx = 0; idx < wgt->children.size; idx++)
        {
            leRectClip(&localRect, rect, &clipRect);

            clipRect.x -= wgt->rect.x;
            clipRect.y -= wgt->rect.y;
            
            invalidateWidget(wgt->children.values[idx], &clipRect);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        wgt->fn->_validateChildren(wgt);
    }
}

static void preWidget(void)
{
    leLayerState* layerState;

    layerState = leGetLayerState(_rendererState.layerIdx);

    // find a dirty widget to render
    _rendererState.currentWidget = findDirtyWidget(&layerState->root.children);
    
    if(_rendererState.currentWidget == NULL)
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTRECT;
    }
    else
    {
        _rendererState.currentWidget->status.drawState = LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_READY;
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_DRAWING;
    }

#if LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE == 1
    if(leGPU_ClearBuffer(&_widgetBuffer) == LE_FAILURE)
    {
        memset(_widgetBufferData,
               0,
               _widgetBuffer.buffer_length);
    }
#endif
}

static leBool paintWidget(leWidget* widget)
{
    leRect clipRect;
    leBool shouldPaint = LE_FALSE;
    
#if LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL >= 1
    leBool painted = LE_FALSE;
#endif
    
    // skip any child that isn't dirty or that does not have a dirty descendant
    if(widget->status.dirtyState == LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_CLEAN)
        return LE_TRUE;
        
    // if widget is completely transparent just mark clean and return
#if LE_ALPHA_BLENDING_ENABLED == 1
    if(widget->fn->getCumulativeAlphaEnabled(widget) == LE_TRUE)
    {
        _rendererState.alphaEnable = LE_TRUE;
        _rendererState.alpha = widget->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount(widget);

        if(_rendererState.alpha == 0)
        {
            widget->fn->_validateChildren(widget);

            return LE_TRUE;
        }
    }
    else
    {
        _rendererState.alphaEnable = LE_FALSE;
        _rendererState.alpha = 0xFF;
    }
#endif
    
    if(widget->status.dirtyState == LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_DIRTY)
    {
        shouldPaint = LE_TRUE;
    }
    
    // paint this widget and clear dirty flag
    if(shouldPaint == LE_TRUE)
    {   
        // clip the damage rectangle to the child's parent
        if(widget->parent != NULL)
        {
            leUtils_ClipRectToAncestors(widget, &clipRect);
            
            // child does not intersect parent at all, do not draw
            if(clipRect.width <= 0 ||
               clipRect.height <= 0)
            {
                widget->fn->_validateChildren(widget);
        
                return LE_TRUE;
            }
            
            // widget visible area does not intersect dirty area at all
            // do not draw
            if(leRectIntersects(&clipRect,
                                &_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList.rects[_rendererState.frameRectIdx]) == LE_FALSE)
            {
                widget->fn->_validateChildren(widget);
        
                return LE_TRUE;
            }
            
            // get the delta area between the dirty area and the child/parent
            // delta area
            leRectClip(&_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList.rects[_rendererState.frameRectIdx],
                       &clipRect,
                       &_rendererState.drawRect);
        }
        else
        {
            _rendererState.drawRect = _rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList.rects[_rendererState.frameRectIdx];
        }

        //printf("rendering frame %i, widget %i, type %i, rect %i %i %i %i\n", _rendererState.drawCount, widget->id, widget->type, widget->rect.x, widget->rect.y, widget->rect.width, widget->rect.height);

        widget->fn->_handleEvent(widget, &paintEvt);
        widget->drawCount++;
        
#if LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL >= 1
        painted = LE_TRUE;
#endif 
        
        //printf("painting widget - %i, %i\n", widget->type, widget->id);
        
        if(widget->status.drawState != LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE)
            return LE_FALSE;
            
        _rendererState.frameDrawCount++;
    }
    
    if(widget->children.size > 0)
    {
        widget->status.dirtyState = LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_CHILD;
    }
    else
    {
        widget->status.dirtyState = LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_CLEAN;
    }

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 00:35:18Z)**_

Here's my honest read after tracing the renderer end to end — I'm not going to hand-wave it as "expected."

**What the code says should happen (layer 0, single layer):**
- `LE_PREEMPTION_LEVEL = 0` → paint completes in one pass (our single-pass `_paint` is correct).
- Per damaged rect, `preRect()` runs `invalidateWidget(layerRoot, rect)` (renderer.c:637), which marks **every** widget intersecting that rect dirty — across sibling subtrees, including our opaque overlay — then the paint walk redraws them bottom-to-top in z-order.
- So an opaque layer-0 widget added *after* the dashboard **should** cover it, even when the dashboard repaints under it.

By that model, `FILL` should have fixed it and it shouldn't bleed. It still does. So I'm **not** comfortable calling this either "expected" or "definitely a Legato bug" yet — the static analysis says it should work, which means either a real Legato edge-case (my prime suspect: multi-buffering of a *runtime-added* overlay over a *continuously-animating* sibling — `bufferCount>1` carries `prevDamageRects`, a path that's easy to get subtly wrong) **or** a coordinate/clip issue in our paint. Layer compositing is ruled out (layer 1's only panel is `setVisible(FALSE)`).

There's one free observation that cleanly splits "our bug" from "library bug," and you can already see it without instrumenting anything:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 00:39:44Z)**_

That symptom pattern is genuinely diagnostic, and it points away from "expected":

- **Static image never bleeds** → it's drawn once and never invalidates, so our overlay stays on top of it. ✓ consistent.
- **Text bleeds where it's under the list, tracks the animation, freezes when animation stops** → the text widgets behind are *repainting*, and our overlay is **not being repainted on top of them** when they do. The "frozen" bleed is just the last animated frame left uncovered.

So the whole pattern reduces to one thing: **our overlay isn't getting repainted when a sibling behind it repaints.** And that is *exactly* the case the renderer's `preRect → invalidateWidget(layerRoot, rect)` is supposed to handle — it dirties every widget intersecting a damaged rect, ours included, with no occlusion check in that path. By the code, our widget should be re-dirtied and redrawn on top. It isn't. So this looks like a **real defect**, not expected behavior — I'm just not yet certain whether it's a Legato damage-propagation gap or something about our widget that excludes it from the dirty walk.

There's a definitive, no-guessing classifier: the renderer increments `widget->drawCount` every time it actually paints a widget (renderer.c, in `paintWidget`). So I'll expose ours and let you watch it while the text animates under the list:

- **drawCount climbs while text animates under it** → our widget *is* being painted but the text still shows → z-order/clip bug on our side (fixable in the widget).
- **drawCount stays flat while text animates** → Legato isn't re-dirtying our cross-subtree overlay on the damaged rect → a library-side gap (and the workaround is structural — own layer/screen, which production already is).

Confirmed (`legato_widget.h:639` — `drawCount` is real, incremented by the renderer per paint), and everything compiles.

## Where this lands

I'm not going to call it a Legato bug *or* dismiss it — but I'll give you my honest lean and a way to **prove** it rather than argue it.

Your symptom pattern reduces cleanly to one statement: **our overlay isn't being repainted when a text widget behind it repaints** (static image = never repaints = never bleeds; animating text = repaints = bleeds; freezes when it stops). And per the renderer code I traced, that's the exact case `preRect → invalidateWidget(layerRoot, rect)` is supposed to cover — it dirties *every* widget intersecting a damaged rect (no occlusion check in that path), and the paint walk redraws them in z-order with our opaque overlay last. So **the code says this should work**, which makes the observed bleed a real anomaly worth your skepticism.

## The test that settles it (added now)

`songlist stats` prints the renderer's own `drawCount` for our widget. Steps:
1. `songlist` (attach), then `songlist stats` — note the number.
2. Let the dashboard text animate under it a few seconds, `songlist stats` again.

- **drawCount climbed** → Legato *is* repainting our widget, but the text still shows → the fault is on our side (z-order / clip / coordinates) and I can fix it in the widget.
- **drawCount flat** → Legato is *not* re-dirtying our overlay on the sibling's damage → a library-side gap in cross-subtree overlap repaint for a runtime-added top-level widget. Then the right answer is structural (own layer/screen), not a widget tweak.

My lean: slightly toward **flat / library-side**, because our paint is dead simple (full opaque fill of the rect, clipped automatically) and the z-order/walk ordering checks out on paper — but I genuinely want the number before committing to that.

Either way, production is unaffected (the real SELECT SONG screen has no animating widgets stacked behind the list). Run `songlist stats` and tell me which way `drawCount` goes — that tells us definitively whether to file/work-around a Legato issue or fix ours.

```text
=== findDirtyWidget (full) ===
static leWidget* findDirtyWidget(leArray* widgetArray)
{
    uint32_t idx;
    leWidget *wgt, *child;
    
    if(widgetArray->size == 0)
        return NULL;
    
    for(idx = 0; idx < widgetArray->size; idx++)
    {
        wgt = widgetArray->values[idx];
        
        if(wgt->status.dirtyState == LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_DIRTY)
        {
            return wgt;
        }
        else if(wgt->status.dirtyState == LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_CHILD)
        {
            child = findDirtyWidget(&wgt->children);
            
            if(child != NULL)
            {            
                return child;
            }
            else
            {
                wgt->status.dirtyState = LE_WIDGET_DIRTY_STATE_CLEAN;
            }
        }
    }
    
    return NULL;
}
=== _postWidget (full) ===
static void _postWidget(void)
{
#if LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE == 1
    if(_gpuBlitWidgetBuffer() == LE_FAILURE)
    {
        _swBlitWidgetBuffer();
    }
#endif
}

static void _nextRect(void)
{
    _rendererState.frameRectIdx += 1;

    if(_rendererState.frameRectIdx < _rendererState.currentRenderLayer->frameRectList.size)
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_PRERECT;
    }
    else
    {
        _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTLAYER;
    }
}
