```text
=== DRV_GFX2D_Fill (full) ===
gfxResult DRV_GFX2D_Fill(gfxPixelBuffer* dest,
                           const gfxRect* clipRect,
                           const gfxColor color)
{
    GFX2D_BUFFER    dest_buffer;
    GFX2D_RECTANGLE dest_rect;
    gfxColor        fill_color;

    if(dest->orientation != GFX_ORIENT_0)
		return GFX_FAILURE;

    dest_buffer.width = dest->size.width;
    dest_buffer.height = dest->size.height;
    dest_buffer.format = gfx2dFormats[dest->mode];
    dest_buffer.dir = GFX2D_XY00;
    dest_buffer.addr = (uint32_t)dest->pixels;

    dest_rect.x = (uint32_t)clipRect->x;
    dest_rect.y = (uint32_t)clipRect->y;
    dest_rect.width = (uint32_t)clipRect->width;
    dest_rect.height = (uint32_t)clipRect->height;

    if (dest->mode == GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565)
    {
        fill_color = gfxColorConvert(dest->mode, GFX_COLOR_MODE_ARGB_8888, color);
    }
    else
    {
        fill_color = color;
    }

    PLIB_GFX2D_Fill(&dest_buffer, &dest_rect, fill_color);

    while(PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy() == true);

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}
=== DRV_GFX2D_Blit (full) ===
gfxResult DRV_GFX2D_Blit(const gfxPixelBuffer* source,
                           const gfxRect* srcRect,
                           const gfxPixelBuffer* dest,
                        const gfxRect* destRect)
{
    GFX2D_BUFFER    dest_buffer;
    GFX2D_RECTANGLE dest_rect;
    GFX2D_BUFFER    src_buffer;
    GFX2D_RECTANGLE src_rect;

    if(source->orientation != GFX_ORIENT_0 ||
       dest->orientation != GFX_ORIENT_0)
		return GFX_FAILURE;

    dest_buffer.width = dest->size.width;
    dest_buffer.height = dest->size.height;
    dest_buffer.format = gfx2dFormats[dest->mode];
    dest_buffer.dir = GFX2D_XY00;
    dest_buffer.addr = (uint32_t)dest->pixels;

    dest_rect.x = (uint32_t)destRect->x;
    dest_rect.y = (uint32_t)destRect->y;
    dest_rect.width = (uint32_t)destRect->width;
    dest_rect.height = (uint32_t)destRect->height;

    src_buffer.width = source->size.width;
    src_buffer.height = source->size.height;
    src_buffer.format = gfx2dFormats[source->mode];
    src_buffer.dir = GFX2D_XY00;
    src_buffer.addr = (uint32_t)source->pixels;

    src_rect.x = (uint32_t)srcRect->x;
    src_rect.y = (uint32_t)srcRect->y;
    src_rect.width = (uint32_t)srcRect->width;
    src_rect.height = (uint32_t)srcRect->height;

	dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source->pixels, source->buffer_length);
	dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(dest->pixels, dest->buffer_length);

    if ( blendState == GFX_BLEND_NONE )
    {
        PLIB_GFX2D_Copy(&dest_buffer, &dest_rect, &src_buffer, &src_rect);
    }
    else
    {
        return GFX_FAILURE;
    }

    while(PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy() == true);

    return GFX_SUCCESS;
}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 02:09:17Z)**_

**Found the smoking gun.** Look at the difference between the two GFX2D operations:

`DRV_GFX2D_Blit` (scratch→framebuffer):
```c
dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source->pixels, source->buffer_length);
dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(dest->pixels, dest->buffer_length);
PLIB_GFX2D_Copy(...);
```

`DRV_GFX2D_Fill`:
```c
PLIB_GFX2D_Fill(&dest_buffer, &dest_rect, fill_color);   // ← NO cache maintenance at all
while(PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy());
```

**`DRV_GFX2D_Fill` has no `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` — `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` does.** That asymmetry explains everything, *if* fills go through the GPU while glyphs are CPU-rendered. The mechanism:

1. CPU software-renders the dashboard **text glyphs** into the scratch → dirty in D-cache, not yet in DDR.
2. Our magenta fill → GFX2D **GPU** writes magenta straight to scratch **DDR** — but does **no cache op**, so the CPU's dirty text lines are untouched in cache.
3. The strip blit (`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`) then does `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source)` — which **writes the CPU's stale text cache lines back to DDR, on top of the GPU's magenta** — then blits that to the framebuffer.

→ text reappears over the fill, at **cache-line granularity** (streaky), **only where CPU-rendered text was** (dirty lines), **intermittent** (eviction timing). That matches every symptom, and it's exactly the kind of thing invisible to the software-logic trace.

One thing left to confirm before declaring it: that Legato fills actually route through `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` (GPU) while glyphs stay CPU. Let me verify.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 02:14:15Z)**_

Now the picture is precise. The active path is:

1. **Fills *and* glyphs are CPU software** — `leRenderer_FillArea → _drawFunction.blendFill → _RGBBlendFill` (legato_draw.c:478). No GPU. So the whole strip (dashboard text + our magenta) is CPU-rendered into the scratch buffer in cached DDR, in correct z-order (magenta over text).
2. **Only the scratch→framebuffer blit is GFX2D**, via `gfxGPUInterface.blitBuffer → DRV_GFX2D_Blit`, which does `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source)` + `(dest)` then `PLIB_GFX2D_Copy`.

So the software render is logically correct, and the corruption is in the **CPU↔GPU cache-coherency at the blit** — exactly the 2D-accelerator layer you suspected. The whole thing hinges on `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` actually flushing the CPU's scratch writes to where the GPU reads. The two prime ways that fails on a Cortex-A5: it doesn't cover the **L2 cache**, or it mishandles **cache-line alignment**. And the scratch buffer being in **cached** DDR is the precondition. Let me check those.

void dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr (volatile void *pAddr, int32_t size)
{
    volatile uint32_t uAddr = (volatile uint32_t)((volatile uint32_t*)pAddr);
    uint32_t uSize = (uint32_t)size;
    uint32_t mva = uAddr & ~(L1_DATA_CACHE_BYTES - 1U);

    while(mva < (uAddr + uSize))
    {
        cp15_dcache_clean_invalidate_mva((uint32_t)mva);
        __DMB();
        mva += L1_DATA_CACHE_BYTES;
    }

    __DSB();

Now it's concrete. The decisive find:

- **`#define LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR`** (renderer.c:132) — **empty.** And `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` (alignment only). So the Legato scratch buffer `_dataBuffers`, despite the `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` name, is in **ordinary cached DDR**.
- The **framebuffer** *is* non-cached: `FB_CACHE_NC = section(".region_nocache")` (xlcdc:59).
- SoC is **ARM926EJ-S** → L1 only; coherency for the cached scratch rests **entirely** on the manual `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` inside `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`.

So the path is: CPU software-renders the strip (text **and** magenta) into a **cached** scratch → those writes live in L1 → `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` must clean-invalidate that scratch so the 2D engine reads correct DDR → GPU copies to the non-cached framebuffer. The streaky, cache-line-granularity, content-dependent bleed is the classic signature of that manual L1 maintenance being **imperfect** (alignment/length/eviction) — which is exactly what you suspected: the 2D-accelerator path's CPU↔GPU coherency.

Confirmed the asymmetry: `frame_buffer` is `FB_CACHE_NC` → **non-cached** (`.region_nocache`), while the Legato scratch is **cached** (`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` is an empty define).

## Summary — where the bug lives

You were right to suspect the 2D accelerator path. The active render pipeline is:

```
CPU software-renders each strip (panels + text + our fill)  →  CACHED scratch buffer  (lives in L1)
        ↓  DRV_GFX2D_Blit:  dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(scratch)  →  PLIB_GFX2D_Copy  →  NON-cached framebuffer
```

So coherency between the CPU-rendered scratch and the 2D engine rests **entirely** on that one manual `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` in `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`. Two concrete defects in that area:

1. **`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` is empty** (legato_renderer.c:132). The scratch buffer is *named* "no cache" and the whole design clearly intends it to be uncached (like the framebuffer driver did with `.region_nocache`), but on this build it's plain cached DDR. The streaky, cache-line-granularity, intermittent, content-dependent bleed is the textbook signature of imperfect manual L1 maintenance on that cached buffer feeding the GPU.

2. **`DRV_GFX2D_Fill` has no cache maintenance at all** — `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` does `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` on src+dest; `Fill` does none. Latent now (core fills are software here), but a real driver bug that bites any GPU-fill config (`LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=1`, etc.). Worth fixing upstream regardless.

## The decisive test (and likely fix)

Make the scratch buffer non-cached, exactly like the framebuffer — point `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` at `.region_nocache`:

```c
/* legato_renderer.c ~line 132 */
#define LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR  __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))
```

If the bleed disappears → it's confirmed: the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, and that's the fix (the scratch should never have been cached; the manual clean-invalidate is a fragile substitute). If it persists, the next probe is the `PLIB_GFX2D_Copy` rect geometry leaving strips of stale framebuffer.

**One honest caveat:** the cache theory cleanly explains *streaky / intermittent / "during draw"*, but I can't fully explain from static reading why it's selectively *text* and not the solid panels — both are CPU-written to the same cached scratch. The non-cached-scratch test will settle that directly (if it's coherency, all of it goes away at once).

Want me to apply that `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` change so you can build and test? It's a one-liner in the Legato renderer source (generated tree, so you'd carry it in your Legato config/MGS rather than let a regen clobber it).

Numbers are in, and the news is good on the budget:

## `.region_nocache` budget (16 MB total)
| Item | Size |
|---|---|
| ISC capture pool (4 × 1280×720×3) | ~10.55 MB |
| Framebuffer (2 layers × 1280×800 × RGB565) | 3.91 MB |
| **+ Legato scratch (this change)** | **0.5 MB** |
| **Total** | **~15.0 MB of 16 MB** |

So it **fits with ~1 MB to spare — no MCC bump needed.** (USB UDPHS has a little nocache too, but that ~1 MB margin covers it.) If the link *does* report `region ram_nocache overflowed`, bump `ram_nocache` LENGTH in `ddram.ld` / via MCC — but you likely won't need to.

## What I changed
`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` (legato_renderer.c:131) now expands to `__attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))` — the same section the framebuffer uses. That moves the CPU-rendered scratch `_dataBuffers` into non-cached DDR, so the 2D engine reads exactly what the CPU wrote, with no reliance on the manual `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr`. (`_widgetBufferData` is behind `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE==1`, off, so it doesn't move; the `_scratchBuffers` *descriptors* stay cached, which is correct — they're CPU-only metadata.)

## Test
Build, then: `songlist` → `songlist solid`.
- **Magenta is now clean (no text streaks)** → confirmed: it was the cached-scratch ↔ 2D-engine coherency, and this is the fix. Then `songlist off` and scroll — the real rows should be clean too.
- **Still bleeds** → coherency wasn't it; next probe is the `PLIB_GFX2D_Copy` rect geometry leaving stale framebuffer strips.

## If it's confirmed, two upstream items for Microchip Legato/gfx
1. **`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` is empty** for this SAM9 (cached-DDR) target — the scratch buffer intended as non-cached is actually cached. The framebuffer driver wired `.region_nocache`; the Legato renderer didn't. (For the permanent fix, define it in `legato_config.h` / the Harmony graphics config so it survives MGS regen rather than living as this hand-edit.)
2. **`DRV_GFX2D_Fill` has no cache maintenance** while `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` does — latent now (core fills are software), but a real bug for any GPU-fill config.

Give it a build and tell me what `songlist solid` shows — fingers crossed the magenta comes up clean.

Confirmed: `CACHE_ALIGN = __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE)` — **alignment only, no section**, so the buffers sit in normal **cacheable** DDR. So your project is currently in the **"Cacheable Frame Buffers = ON"** mode, and you've read it exactly right:

- **ON (current):** `LE_COHERENT_ATTR = CACHE_ALIGN` → cacheable, cache-line-aligned buffers, and the GFX2D driver carries the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` maintenance to keep them coherent with the 2D engine. Faster CPU rendering (cache-speed pixel writes), **but correctness depends entirely on that maintenance being right — and it isn't** (the scratch coherency leaked, and `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` has no maintenance at all).
- **OFF:** buffers go in a non-cached section, no maintenance needed — which is exactly what your `.region_nocache` edit emulated, and it fixed it.

So **yes, non-cacheable (OFF) is the better option here**, for the reasons you'd expect on an ARM926 with a DMA-driven 2D engine + a display reading straight from DDR: it removes the fragile manual cache-maintenance dependency entirely. The only thing the cacheable path buys you is render speed, and it's currently broken.

**The one tradeoff** (so it's on the record): non-cached means CPU software rendering writes straight to DDR with no write-back coalescing — slower glyph/fill rendering. For a mostly-static operator UI with occasional scrolling, that's almost certainly a non-issue; if you ever build a heavily-animated screen you'd feel it. But "correct and simple" beats "fast and broken."

**Suggested path:**
1. Flip **"Cacheable Frame Buffers" OFF** in MCC, regenerate.
2. Verify the regenerated `legato_config.h` `LE_COHERENT_ATTR` (and/or `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR`) now place the Legato render/scratch buffers in non-cached memory.
3. If it does → **drop my hand-edit** to `legato_renderer.c:131` (the MCC setting is the proper, regen-surviving home — exactly what I flagged earlier about not letting a patch linger in the generated tree).
4. Re-test `songlist solid` to confirm it's still clean.

One thing worth verifying post-regen: the **framebuffer** was already non-cached via the XLCDC driver's hardcoded `FB_CACHE_NC` (display-DMA coherency requirement) **independent** of this option — that's why the FB was fine but the Legato scratch wasn't. They're controlled separately; turning the option off should bring the Legato buffers in line with the FB.

And with your Legato-dev hat on — independent of this product's choice, the **cacheable path has two real bugs** worth fixing upstream so "ON" is actually safe for everyone:
1. `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` is missing the `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` that `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` has.
2. The cacheable scratch coherency leaked even *with* the Blit's maintenance — so the clean-invalidate sequence/coverage for a CPU-software-rendered, then GPU-blitted, scratch buffer isn't sufficient on this SoC. That's the one that actually bit us, and it'd bite any cacheable-mode user doing software glyph rendering + GPU blit.

Short answer: **no.** And the reason is worth being precise about, because it tells you where the real fix is.

Two facts from the trace:

1. **`DRV_GFX2D_Fill` is never called in this path.** With `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE=0`, Legato's fills (including our magenta) and glyphs are **CPU software** — `leRenderer_FillArea → _drawFunction.blendFill → _RGBBlendFill`. The only GPU operation in the whole song-list render is the scratch→framebuffer **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`**. So adding cache maintenance to `Fill` can't affect a path that doesn't use it. (Fill's missing invalidate is a real *latent* bug — it'd bite if you turned on the GPU-fill/widget-buffer path — but it's orthogonal to this.)

2. **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit` already has the cache invalidate** (`dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr` on source + dest) — and it **still bled**. So "a GPU op is missing the invalidate" isn't the failure mode here. The failure is that the existing source-side maintenance over the **cached** scratch isn't actually keeping it coherent with the 2D engine's read.

That's why non-cached scratch fixed it and patching Fill wouldn't: you removed the dependency on that maintenance entirely, rather than adding more of the same maintenance that was already there and already insufficient.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 02:45:26Z)**_

Confirmed the coverage is actually correct: the blit passes `gfxBuffer.buffer_length = renderBuffer.buffer_length = width*height*bpp` (the strip extent), and `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` cleans exactly that range — i.e., it cleans precisely the bytes the CPU rendered. So it's **not** a short/missing invalidate that more maintenance would fix.

So to your question — **no**, and here's the crisp reasoning:

1. **`DRV_GFX2D_Fill` isn't on this path** — fills are CPU software (`_RGBBlendFill`), so patching Fill changes nothing here. (It's a real latent bug for GPU-fill configs, just not this one.)
2. **The op that *is* on the path (`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`) already does the clean-invalidate, over the correct range, and it still leaked.** So the failure isn't "a GPU op is missing cache maintenance" — it's that the cache-maintenance path *itself* doesn't reliably keep a CPU-rendered **cached** scratch coherent with the 2D engine on this SoC. Adding the same kind of maintenance to Fill would just be more of the thing that already wasn't sufficient.

The most telling evidence is what Microchip already did with the **framebuffer**: it's placed in `.region_nocache` (`FB_CACHE_NC`) rather than relying on cache maintenance — i.e., for a GPU-touched, DMA-read buffer on this ARM926/2D-engine combo, the chosen-and-trusted policy is *non-cached*, not *cached + clean-invalidate*. The scratch is the same kind of buffer (CPU writes it, 2D engine reads it) and should follow the same policy. The bug is simply that the generator applied that policy to the framebuffer but not to the Legato render buffer.

So:
- **Right fix:** non-cached scratch (what you did) — aligns the scratch with the framebuffer's proven non-cache policy and removes the maintenance dependency entirely.
- **Adding invalidate to Fill:** doesn't touch this path, and even on its own path it's the weaker strategy (relying on maintenance the framebuffer deliberately avoids). Still worth fixing upstream for correctness of GPU-fill configs, but it won't fix this.

If you specifically wanted to *keep* the scratch cacheable for software-render speed, the thing to chase would be **why `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`'s source clean-invalidate is insufficient on this SoC** (write-buffer drain / 2D-engine bus-master coherency / an ARM926 cache nuance) — not Fill. But given Microchip already answers that question for the framebuffer by going non-cached, matching that for the scratch is the lower-risk, consistent fix.

Custom Legato widget for the SELECT SONG setlist (spec §4.8): a
hand-written leWidget subclass (ui/song_list.{h,c}) — the stock list
widget is disabled and can't render the tier-badge + two-line +
right-aligned-duration row. Decoupled via a row-provider callback (no
game/catalog.h dependency); drag scroll with time-based kinetic inertia
off the FreeRTOS tick (Legato's leUpdate passes dt=0, so we measure real
elapsed time ourselves); tap-to-select with a selection callback;
virtualized software paint (RectFill + DrawCString) so there are no
per-row child widgets. Single pool allocation; the vtable is built by
copying the base vtable at runtime (project builds LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES=0,
so _leWidget_FillVTable isn't linkable). Declared opaque (FILL) so Legato
composits it correctly.

Bring-up scaffolding (ui/song_list_demo.{c,h}) wires a catalog-backed
provider + a `songlist` console command (attach/off/hide/show/solid/
tree/stats) to exercise scroll/inertia/select on the live screen before
the MGS song-select screen exists. Temporary; removed once that screen
lands.

user.cmake: define LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR = section(".region_nocache") to place
the Legato render scratch in non-cached DDR (pairs with the 32 MB region
bump). Works around an MGS gen gap — with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" off
the framebuffer is non-cached but the Legato scratch is left cacheable,
so the GFX2D blit reads stale CPU-cached pixels and bleeds underlying
content through the widget. The #ifndef guard in legato_renderer.c lets
this -D win and survive MGS regen, keeping it out of the generated tree.

Widget validated on hardware (smooth scroll, select, clean opaque fill).

The ISC capture buffers are DMA-aligned already, but app-side staging buffers are the risk. Speed-mode-DEFAULT is *not* the bottleneck (reads prove the link); revisit High-Speed mode only if aligned writes still fall short of the §4.6.2 ≥5 MB/s target. |

```md
# Harmony Graphics (Legato) — cache-coherency bugs with the GFX2D 2D engine on cached-DDR SoCs

**Status:** confirmed + fixed via workaround on hardware.
**Target:** SAM9X75 (SAM9X7 family, ARM926EJ-S, L1-only — no L2), Harmony Graphics / Legato, GFX2D 2D Graphics Engine, XLCDC display controller. Single-buffered (`XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER = 1`). **Graphics driver option "Cacheable Frame Buffers" = OFF.**

> File/line references below are to the MHC-generated component sources; the
> bugs are in the library/driver/generator, not in the application.

---

## TL;DR

With **"Cacheable Frame Buffers" OFF**, the generator correctly places the **XLCDC framebuffer** in non-cached memory but leaves the **Legato render/scratch buffer cacheable**. The CPU software-renders the frame into that cached scratch; the GFX2D 2D engine then blits scratch→framebuffer; the driver's manual D-cache maintenance does not keep the cached scratch coherent with the 2D engine on ARM926. Result: **stale CPU-cached pixels blit through** — a streaky, intermittent, content-dependent corruption (in our case, underlying widgets bled *through* an opaque widget drawn on top of them).

Two distinct defects:

1. **(Primary)** "Cacheable Frame Buffers = OFF" does not make the **Legato render/scratch buffer** non-cached — only the framebuffer. The scratch stays cacheable, and the manual cache maintenance around the GFX2D blit is insufficient.
2. **(Latent)** `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` performs **no** D-cache maintenance, whereas `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` does. Any config that routes fills through the GPU (e.g. `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE = 1`) will hit this.

---

## Symptom

Drawing an **opaque** widget on top of existing content (same layer), the content *underneath* bled through the opaque widget:

- **Streaky / intermittent**, at roughly cache-line granularity.
- **Only where CPU-rendered text** sat underneath; large solid fills underneath did not visibly bleed.
- Correlated with the overlay's own repaint; "froze" when repainting stopped.
- A **bare opaque rectangle fill** (no text, no child widgets) drawn by the overlay still showed the bleed → not an application z-order / coverage issue.

## Diagnosis (by elimination)

The software render logic is correct — pre-order paint composites the opaque overlay last, so by the code it should fully cover. The bug is below the software layer:

- Layer colour mode is RGB_565 (no alpha) → fills are unconditionally opaque. Not an alpha bug.
- `XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER = 1` → not a double-buffer / `prevDamageRects` bug.
- Overlay confirmed top-most child of the rendered root (z-order correct).
- **Decisive tests:** (a) a bare opaque magenta rect still bled; (b) hiding the underlying content cleared it; (c) **moving the Legato scratch buffer to non-cached memory eliminated it entirely.**

→ It is the cached scratch buffer ↔ GFX2D 2D-engine coherency.

---

## The render path (this configuration)

`LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE = 0`, so:

1. **CPU software** renders every widget (fills *and* glyphs) into the Legato **scratch buffer**:
   `leRenderer_FillArea() → _drawFunction.blendFill = _RGBBlendFill` (software), and glyphs via the software string renderer. (`legato_draw.c`, `legato_draw_rect.c`)
2. Per damaged strip, `postRect()` blits the scratch buffer to the framebuffer via the display driver:
   `dispDriver->blitBuffer()` → XLCDC `blitBuffer()` → `gfxGPUInterface.blitBuffer` = **`DRV_GFX2D_Blit`**. (`legato_renderer.c`, `drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`, `drv_gfx2d.c`)

So the **only** GPU operation in the active path is the scratch→framebuffer **blit**. Coherency of the CPU-rendered scratch with the 2D engine rests entirely on the manual D-cache maintenance inside `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`.

---

## Bug 1 (primary): "Cacheable Frame Buffers = OFF" leaves the Legato render buffer cacheable

The **framebuffer** is correctly non-cached (XLCDC driver):

\```c
/* drv_gfx_xlcdc.c */
#define FB_CACHE_NC  __attribute__ ((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))
FB_BPP_TYPE FB_CACHE_NC frame_buffer[XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS * XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER][XLCDC_HOR_RES * XLCDC_VER_RES];
\```

But the **Legato render/scratch buffer is cacheable**:

\```c
/* legato_renderer.c */
#ifndef LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR
#define LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR              /* <-- emitted EMPTY */
#endif
...
static uint8_t LE_COHERENT_ATTR LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR __ALIGNED(64)
    _dataBuffers[LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT][SCRATCH_BUFFER_SZ];
\```

\```c
/* legato_config.h (generated) */
#define LE_COHERENT_ATTR   CACHE_ALIGN          /* alignment only */
/* toolchain_specifics.h */
#define CACHE_ALIGN        __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE)
\```

So `_dataBuffers` is in ordinary **cacheable** DDR, despite the `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` name and despite "Cacheable Frame Buffers" being **off**. The CPU's render writes live in L1; `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`'s `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source,...)` is the sole coherency mechanism, and on this ARM926 + 2D-engine combination it does not reliably keep the buffer coherent (the corruption is at cache-line granularity, content-dependent, intermittent — the classic signature of insufficient/late maintenance feeding a DMA/GPU master).

**Expected:** with "Cacheable Frame Buffers" off (or generally on a target where the framebuffer is non-cached), the Legato render/scratch buffers should be placed in the **same non-cached section** as the framebuffer — i.e. the generator should emit `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` (and/or `LE_COHERENT_ATTR`) as `__attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))`, matching `FB_CACHE_NC`. The buffers are the same *kind* of object (CPU-written, GPU/DMA-read); they should share the same cache policy. Microchip already chose non-cached for the framebuffer rather than trusting cache maintenance — the scratch should follow suit.

---

## Bug 2 (latent): `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` has no cache maintenance

`DRV_GFX2D_Blit` cleans/invalidates both buffers before the GPU op; `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` does not:

\```c
/* drv_gfx2d.c — Blit */
dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(source->pixels, source->buffer_length);
dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(dest->pixels,   dest->buffer_length);
PLIB_GFX2D_Copy(&dest_buffer, &dest_rect, &src_buffer, &src_rect);
while (PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy() == true);
\```

\```c
/* drv_gfx2d.c — Fill (NO cache maintenance) */
PLIB_GFX2D_Fill(&dest_buffer, &dest_rect, fill_color);
while (PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy() == true);
\```

Not exercised in our config (core fills are software), but it will corrupt any path that routes fills through the GPU (`LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE = 1`, or applications calling the fill via `gfxGPUInterface`), in the same cached-buffer scenario. At minimum the two ops should be symmetric.

---

## Reproduction

1. SAM9X7 / ARM926, XLCDC + GFX2D, **"Cacheable Frame Buffers" OFF**, `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE = 0`, single-buffered.
2. Draw any static content (text-heavy) on a layer.
3. Draw an **opaque** widget on top of part of it and repaint it.
4. Observe the underlying text bleeding through the opaque widget, streaky/intermittent.

(Our case: a custom `leWidget` subclass that paints an opaque background + text; reproduced even with a bare opaque `leRenderer_RectFill` of the whole widget rect.)

---

## Fixes

**Bug 1 (generator / library):** When the framebuffer is non-cached, emit the Legato render-buffer cache attribute as the non-cache section too. Concretely, generate

\```c
#define LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR  __attribute__((section(".region_nocache")))
\```

(or point `LE_COHERENT_ATTR` at the non-cache section) for the `_dataBuffers` / `_widgetBufferData` scratch buffers, matching `FB_CACHE_NC`. Today `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` is only an empty `#ifndef` fallback in `legato_renderer.c`, never defined by the generator.

**Bug 2 (driver):** Add the missing `dcache_CleanInvalidateByAddr(dest->pixels, dest->buffer_length)` to `DRV_GFX2D_Fill`, symmetric with `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`.

**General:** On ARM926 (and cached-DDR Cortex-A without coherent GPU masters), prefer **non-cached** graphics buffers for anything the 2D engine / display DMA reads — the non-cached policy already used for the framebuffer is the robust one; the cacheable + manual-maintenance path proved insufficient here.

---

## Workaround we applied (product side)

Define `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` via the project build (the `#ifndef` guard in `legato_renderer.c` lets a `-D` win, so it survives MHC regen and needs no edit to generated sources):

\```cmake
target_compile_definitions(<target> PRIVATE
    "LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR=__attribute__((section(\".region_nocache\")))")
\```

…and enlarge the non-cached DRAM region to fit the scratch buffer. This places `_dataBuffers` in non-cached DDR and **fully eliminates** the bleed (confirmed on hardware).

**Trade-off:** CPU software rendering into non-cached DDR is slower (no write-back coalescing). Acceptable for our mostly-static operator UI; for animation-heavy UIs the better long-term answer is a *correct* cacheable + maintenance path (fix the maintenance), but non-cached is the safe default.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 03:45:22Z)**_

Confirmed against your tree. Here's what `LE_WIDGET_BUFFER_ENABLE` does.

## What it is
An optional **per-widget intermediate render buffer** + composite step. When **on**, each widget is painted into its own off-screen RGBA8888 buffer, then that buffer is **alpha-composited** onto the strip scratch — instead of the widget drawing straight into the scratch.

## How it works here
- **Draw target switch** — `getRenderBuffer()` (renderer.c:198) returns `&_widgetBuffer` when the flag is on, else the strip's `renderBuffer`. So with it on, a widget's paint lands in `_widgetBuffer`, not the shared scratch.
- **Clear before each widget** — `preWidget()` clears `_widgetBuffer` (`leGPU_ClearBuffer`, memset fallback) so each widget starts on a clean transparent canvas.
- **Composite after each widget** — `_postWidget()` blends the widget buffer onto the strip scratch: `_gpuBlitWidgetBuffer()` does a GPU `SRC_OVER` blit using the widget's **cumulative alpha** (`setGlobalAlpha`), with `_swBlitWidgetBuffer()` (per-pixel src-over) as the no-GPU fallback.
- The widget buffer is **RGBA8888** regardless of the layer's color mode (RGB_565 here) — it needs the alpha channel to composite.

## Why it exists
Correct **widget-level (cumulative) alpha / opacity**. To fade or make translucent a *whole widget* — including its background and all its children — as one layer, you render it to its own RGBA buffer and blend that buffer once at the widget's alpha. Without the widget buffer, alpha is applied per draw-primitive into the scene directly, which double-blends where children/background overlap and can't treat a widget+children subtree as a single translucent unit. So it's the "render-to-texture then alpha-composite" path for widgets.

## Costs (why it's off in your config)
- An extra **RGBA8888 buffer** (`_widgetBufferData`, `SCRATCH_BUFFER_SZ` = 512 KB here).
- An extra **clear + composite per widget**, really meant to run on the **GPU** (the software fallback is slow).
- You're driving an opaque RGB_565 operator UI with no widget-level translucency, so the simpler direct-to-scratch path is correct and cheaper — hence `0`.

## Relation to the cache bug we just fixed
Orthogonal to *that* bug (which was the strip scratch being cached), but it expands the same coherency surface if you ever turn it **on**:
- `_widgetBufferData` carries the **same `LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR`** attribute (renderer.c:152) — currently the empty no-op, so it'd be **cacheable** too and need the same non-cache fix.
- The composite goes through the **GPU** (`_gpuBlitWidgetBuffer` → `gpuDriver->blitBuffer` + `setBlend`), so the GFX2D cache-maintenance correctness (incl. **Bug 2**, `DRV_GFX2D_Fill` missing maintenance, and the `leGPU_ClearBuffer` path) becomes load-bearing.

So enabling it on this SoC would mean: non-cache *both* buffers, and make sure every GFX2D op in that path does proper D-cache maintenance — exactly the two issues in the upstream report. For your current UI you don't need it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 03:50:08Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 03:50:27Z)**_

Good questions — and they connect directly to what we just learned. Here's the rundown, grounded in this renderer.

## What the scratch buffer is for
Legato renders **damaged regions, off-screen, then blits the finished result to the framebuffer**. Per frame: `preLayer` turns the dirty rects into a list, **crops them into strips that each fit the scratch** (`maxScratchPixels = SCRATCH_BUFFER_SZ*8 / bpp`), then for each strip it renders all intersecting widgets into the scratch (`getRenderBuffer()` → the scratch) and `DRV_GFX2D_Blit`s that strip to the framebuffer.

So the scratch is the **staging/compositing area**. Its value, even for your UI:

1. **Clean updates on a single, continuously-scanned framebuffer.** Your XLCDC framebuffer is being scanned out by display DMA the whole time, and it's single-buffered (`XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER=1`). Rendering a strip off-screen and committing it with one fast GPU blit makes each region's old→new transition near-atomic, instead of the scanout catching half-drawn widgets.
2. **Correct multi-widget compositing** of a damaged region (back-to-front, blends, overlaps) before it's written.
3. **Bounded render working set** — the renderer only ever works on one strip-sized buffer regardless of screen size.

## Why not render straight to the framebuffer
You essentially *can* (composite directly into the FB), but on a single-buffered, actively-scanned framebuffer that means the display sees every intermediate step — background clear, then each widget appearing one by one → **tearing/flicker**. And you lose clean overlap/alpha compositing. The scratch+blit is the lighter-weight stand-in for double-buffering: you pay one cheap GPU strip-copy to avoid rendering *in* the buffer the LCD is reading. (Note: with the scratch now non-cached too, it costs no more per-pixel than the FB would; the only extra is the blit, which is GPU and fast.)

## Increasing scratch **size** — yes, real value (and cheap now)
Bigger scratch → bigger `maxScratchPixels` → **fewer, larger strips** per damaged region → fewer blits + less per-strip overhead (each strip costs an `invalidateWidget` tree walk, a GPU blit setup, and cache/clear work). Concretely at your 512 KB / RGB565:
- `maxScratchPixels` ≈ 262 K px.
- Full screen (1280×800 = 1.02 M px) → ~**4 strips**; your song list (560×640 = 358 K px) → **2 strips**.
- Bump to **~1 MB** → the list repaints in **1 strip**; **2 MB** → the *whole screen* in 1 strip.

With the nocache region now at 32 MB, that's free headroom. It **won't** speed up the per-pixel software render (same pixels either way), but it cuts the fixed per-strip overhead — worthwhile for the scrolling list, which redraws its whole rect every frame. Sweet spot: size it to the largest single thing you repaint so it's one strip.

## Increasing scratch **count** — little value *here*
Multiple scratch buffers exist to **pipeline**: CPU renders strip N+1 while the GPU blits strip N (`preRect` picks an unlocked buffer). But in this driver `DRV_GFX2D_Blit` is **synchronous** — it ends with `while (PLIB_GFX2D_GetGlobalStatusBusy());`, blocking until the GPU finishes. So the CPU already waits for each blit; a second scratch has nothing to overlap with. Count > 1 only pays off if the blit becomes **non-blocking** (fire-and-continue), at which point double-buffering the scratch would overlap render and blit. As-is, leave it at 1.

**Net recommendation:** keep one scratch, but consider bumping `LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB` so your list (and ideally the full screen) renders in a single strip — cheap given 32 MB nocache, and it trims per-frame overhead on the scrolling path. Count stays 1 unless/until the GFX2D blit path goes async.
